items.jobDescription:
Afin d'accompagner notre constante croissance et nos 250 000 clients dans le monde, nous recherchons un Consultant en réalisation de projets Modélisation & Simulation passionné pour intégrer notre équipe de services. Ce poste, basé à Vélizy-Villacoublay, offre l'opportunité de contribuer à des projets ambitieux dans un environnement dynamique au sein du CATIA HUB, centre de compétence international.
 Missions
 Accompagner les clients dans le déploiement des solutions CATIA Cyber Systems
 Contribuer à la croissance des clients existants par le soutien, la formation et le mentorat
 Contribuer à l'élaboration et à la livraison de matériel de formation et d'informations techniques orientées utilisateur
 Assurer la liaison entre les clients et la R&D pour assurer une résolution rapide des problèmes
 Développer des compétences sur les nouvelles solutions et les nouvelles versions et passer les Certifications
 Transférer les compétences en partageant les connaissances techniques en interne et avec les partenaires
 Contribuer à la communauté technique DS à travers la Capitalisation/le partage des connaissances et les publications
 Concevoir, développer et maintenir des modèles et simulateurs de systèmes complexes dans différents domaines, et notamment ferroviaires et industrie manufacturière
 Développer et intégrer des briques logicielles de simulation conformes aux exigences clients
 Rédiger et exécuter les spécifications techniques, plans de tests et scénarios de validation des modèles développés
 Exécuter les campagnes de tests et de validation par scénarios, et produire les rapports associés (traçabilité des exigences, résultats de simulation, analyse d'écarts)
 Déboguer, analyser et corriger les anomalies détectées lors des phases de vérification et de validation
 Documenter les modèles, le code et les procédures afin de garantir la maintenabilité et la réutilisabilité des livrables
 Collaborer au quotidien avec l'équipe projet, les consultants seniors et le manager de réalisation pour assurer la livraison clé en main des projets de simulation
 Contribuer à l'amélioration continue des outils, frameworks et bibliothèques de modélisation de l'équipe
 Qualifications
 Professionnel expérimenté dans la modélisation et simulation de systèmes complexes.
Expertise pratique dans l'application du cycle en V, avec une attention particulière portée aux activités de vérification et de validation : traçabilité des exigences, écriture et exécution de plans de tests, validation par scénarios.
Rigoureux, autonome et orienté systèmes, garantissant des solutions fiables et conformes dans le secteur des transports et de l'industrie manufacturière.
 Diplôme de Master ou d'ingénieur en ingénierie systèmes , automatique, systèmes embarqués ou similaire
 Expérience avérée du développement logiciel des systèmes embarqués (C/C++, Python, JAVA, ou langages similaires) et/ou des système automatisés (IEC 61131) et des protocoles de communication associés
 Solide expérience pratique de la modélisation et de la simulation de systèmes, ainsi que de la mise en œuvre des outils et méthodologies associés (par exemple ControlBuild, Dymola, Matlab/Simulink, Scade)
 Bonne maîtrise et application concrète du cycle de vie en V, avec un accent sur les activités de vérification et de validation
 Expérience en gestion des exigences (DOORS ou équivalent), écriture de plans de tests, exécution de campagnes de tests, vérification et validation des systèmes
 Capacité à travailler en équipe au sein de projets d'ingénierie pluridisciplinaires, sous la coordination d'un chef de projet
 Sens de l'organisation, rigueur dans la documentation et le reporting de son activité
 Optionnellement, connaissances approfondies du secteur ferroviaire, notamment sur les infrastructures et le matériel roulant
 Optionnellement, Connaissance des normes industrielles et des réglementations de sécurité
 Excellentes capacités de communication, de résolution de problèmes et d'interaction technique avec les parties prenantes
 Maîtrise du Français et de l'Anglais professionnel
 Nous rejoindre, c'est aussi
 Intégrer une entreprise scientifique au cœur de l’innovation technologique, portée par une forte croissance depuis plus de 40 ans.
Principaux avantages et bénéfices :
 Environnement multiculturel
 Cadre de travail convivial axé sur le bien-être et la santé (salles de sport & de musique, conciergerie, …)
 Engagement en faveur de la diversité et de l’inclusion
 Politique dynamique de développement de carrière : plan de formation, mobilités internes, etc.
 Inclusion statement
As a game-changer in sustainable technology and innovation, Dassault Systèmes is striving to build more inclusive and diverse teams across the globe. We believe that our people are our number one asset and we want all employees to feel empowered to bring their whole selves to work every day. It is our goal that our people feel a sense of pride and a passion for belonging. As a company leading change, it’s our responsibility to foster opportunities for all people to participate in a harmonized Workforce of the Future.

TLDR; Davis is hiring an AI Engineer to work on the multi-agent pipeline turning raw, fragmented data into expert-grade real estate deliverables. You will make it more reliable, fast, and indistinguishable from the best human teams, then push it past what any human team could do, owning the stack end to end, from context engineering and orchestration to verification, storage and evaluation.
 About Davis 
 Davis is an AI-native real estate company accelerating early-stage development and architectural design. Today developers coordinate 4-5 fragmented stakeholders over weeks or months. Soon they'll need only one: Davis.
 We turn every input that shapes a development decision into decision-ready outputs: investor-grade feasibility studies, investment analysis, and architect-certified designs, delivered in days. Every stage pairs our proprietary AI systems with expert review, so velocity never comes at the cost of reliability.
 We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital , with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneur First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.
 Where We Operate 
 Early-stage development starts with a chain of high-stakes decisions , each requiring different data, different expertise, and different deliverables. Today, we deliver AI-powered outputs across the full spectrum - site sourcing, feasibility studies, architectural design, investment analysis, financial modeling, dataroom analysis, and more.
 The Role 
 You will work on one of the core systems behind what Davis delivers. Our agents take raw, fragmented data and turn it into deliverables that real estate professionals use to make high-stakes decisions. Your job is to make that pipeline reliable, fast, and indistinguishable from work done by the best human teams - then push it beyond what any human team could do.
 You can expect to:
 Build and operate multi-agent systems that turn heterogeneous data into expert-grade deliverables across real estate development workflows.
 Own the system end to end : infra, orchestration, context engineering, how the system selects, structures, and injects the right information so agents behave reliably at scale.
 Ensure production-grade quality , performance, and reliability across every output we deliver to clients.
 Sit with clients and domain experts regularly to understand their constraints, challenge your own assumptions, and make sure every output meets and even exceeds clients' expectations.
 Beyond the technical depth, this role will expose you to how real estate decisions are made, how clients think, and what it takes to deliver outputs they trust. You'll develop a sharp business intuition alongside your engineering skills.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Harness engineering: design and build the system layer around the model - context assembly, tool orchestration, verification, and report generation - to deliver consistent, high-quality outputs at scale.
 Data ingestion & context assembly: handle messy, unstructured project data from heterogeneous sources and ensure agents have the right context at all times.
 Storage & traceability: persist sources, extracted facts, intermediate results, report versions, and expert edits.
 Expert-in-the-loop UX: design and build the review experience (annotations, edits, approvals, diffs/version history, provenance display).
 Evaluation & benchmarking: build an internal eval harness (datasets, rubrics, regression tests, monitoring) to track agents performance over time.
 What We're Looking For 
 1.5+ years building and deploying production software at scale (APIs, reliability, testing, performance).
 Experience building and evaluating LLM agents / multi-step workflows in real systems.
 Proven context engineering experience: you've built systems where reliability depends on assembling the right context (RAG over heterogeneous sources, summarization, conversation state, tool outputs).
 Deep Python expertise (clean architecture, typing, async/concurrency, strong testing culture).
 Strong experience with databases + data modeling (structured storage, document storage, versioning).
 Full-stack experience (you can ship a real UI), with a clear backend emphasis .
 Comfortable building from first principles: we don't want heavy agent frameworks — we prefer a lightweight, well-engineered codebase.
 Nice to Have 
 Experience operating LLM systems with observability and quality monitoring in production.
 GIS familiarity (parcels, zoning layers, geocoding).
 Multi-country product experience (heterogeneous sources, localization, varying rules).
 NLP background
 Why Join Us 
 You're joining a team of 9 at the very beginning - where every decision you make shapes the product, the culture, and the trajectory of the company. What you build here will be yours.
 Direct impact on growth: your work doesn't sit behind three layers of review. You ship, clients use it, and you see the results. Every output you improve translates directly into revenue and reputation.
 Real-world impact : your work supports investment decisions, accelerates development timelines, and helps redefine how cities are imagined, designed, and built.
 High ownership : own the full feasibility stack end to end, as the CEO of that part.
 Competitive salary and meaningful equity in an early-stage company.
 A small team with high standards - we ship fast and love working together.
 More information about Davis, the team and the market we’re going after: 
 Team 
 Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He's a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20 , and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis . They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.
 Today we're a team of 12 : technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise.
 We're small with an extremely high bar . If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you're the one we need.
 Why We'll Win 
 Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.
 Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It didn't work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We don't sell tools, we sell the work: AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.
 Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design Yet 
 Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability ; parametric tools only check constraints after generation , leading to designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.
 Generative AI has the potential to solve this , but doesn't yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. As a result, floorplans may “look” plausible but break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they're usable.
 We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV. 
 If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

 Our Mission 
 We build a foundation model for architectural design that generates compliant, editable building layouts from scratch.  What you'll own:
 Model Architecture & Design Space: Design the core model architecture and work on a discrete design space for architectural layouts. You will choose how to represent floorplans (e.g. as graphs of rooms/connections or token grids) such that the diffusion model’s outputs are editable and code-compliant by construction. This involves ensuring the model can enforce architectural rules (e.g. room sizes, adjacency constraints) within its generation process.
 Large-Scale Model Training: Lead the training of a foundation diffusion model from scratch on GPU clusters. You’ll set up distributed training across multiple nodes, optimize data loading and checkpointing, and manage experiments at scale. The role requires hands-on engineering for efficient training of large models on high-performance computing infrastructure.
 Benchmarking & Iteration: Evaluate the model’s performance and establish benchmarks to measure success. Using these evaluations, you’ll iterate on the model to push performance beyond existing methods. Our goal is to surpass the latest research results and produce genuinely useful architectural designs.

 Applied Research Excellence: PhD or Master’s in Maths, Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Strong foundations in ML and a track record of innovative research, publications, or high-impact projects.
 Diffusion Model Expertise: Deep understanding of diffusion models (discrete or continuous), guided generation techniques, and the latest advances in generative modeling.
 Large-Scale Model Training: Proven experience training large-scale deep learning models on GPU clusters. Comfortable with distributed training, multi-node jobs, experiment management, and handling large datasets.

 Research Literacy: Ability to read, evaluate, and implement advanced ML research. You stay current with state-of-the-art generative modeling work and can adapt cutting-edge methods to domain-specific problems.
 Collaboration & Communication: Strong teamwork skills. Able to articulate complex concepts clearly and work closely with AI engineers, researchers, and domain experts to integrate technical solutions into the architectural design workflow.
 Nice to Have 
 Industry Experience: Background in a top AI research organization or cutting-edge startup, especially working on foundation models or generative AI tools.
 Publications/Open Source: Research publications in generative modeling (diffusion, VAEs, flows, GANs) or significant open-source contributions demonstrating ability to push state-of-the-art systems.
 Domain Knowledge: While not required, an interest in architecture or design will help.
 Reinforcement Learning & Optimization: Experience with RL, reward modeling, or constrained optimization (particularly MCTS, GRPO and RLHF) relevant to guiding generative models under complex constraints.
 Multimodal Generation: Experience with graph-based, sequence-based, or discrete structured generative models (e.g., molecule generation, layout generation, program synthesis) or with graph neural networks.
 Why Join Us 
 You're joining a team of 12 at the very beginning - where every decision you make shapes the product, the culture, and the trajectory of the company. What you build here will be yours.
 Build what no one has before : the foundation model that automates architectural design and redefines how cities are imagined, designed, and built.

 We're small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you're the one we need.
 Why We'll Win 
 Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.
 Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It didn't work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We don't sell tools, we sell the work: AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.
 Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design Yet 
 Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability ; parametric tools only check constraints after generation , leading to designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.
 Generative AI has the potential to solve this , but doesn't yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. As a result, floorplans may “look” plausible but break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they're usable.
 We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV. 
 If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.
 The Role 
 We are looking for applied AI engineers to build AI-native systems for BJAK's AI Neobank app.
This is not a research-only role. We need builders who can use AI to automate real workflows, improve products, reduce manual work and make financial services easier for users and teams.
 What You Will Build

 What We Look For

 Experience building AI agents, LLM apps, RAG systems, automation workflows, copilots or AI-enabled tools.

 Fintech, banking, support automation, risk, KYC, fraud, CRM or operations automation experience is a strong plus.
 This Role Is Not For 
 People who only want research projects with no production ownership.
 Candidates who treat AI as demos instead of working systems.

 People who overclaim AI impact without evidence.
 Builders who cannot work with product, ops and business teams.
 The Bar

 Location 
 This role is based in the UK . This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our UK office at least 3 days per week.
 Language 
 English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.
 Interview Process

class="jobdescription"> Innovative Technologielösungen entwickeln und diese in die Anwendung bringen – das ist unser Ziel am Fraunhofer-Institut für Photonische Mikrosysteme IPMS .

items.jobTitle: Staff Platform Engineer - Core Platform Engineering
items.jobDescription:
Title: Staff Platform Engineer
 Department: Platform & Release Engineering
 Location: Espoo, Finland / Berlin, Germany
 Reports to: Infrastructure Engineering Lead
 Employment type: Permanent
 Workplace model: Hybrid
 Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO)
 Why This Role Matters
 As a Senior / Staff Platform Engineer, you’ll own and evolve the foundations that all services rely on, leading the design and operation of a secure, scalable Kubernetes platform across cloud and on-prem environments so product teams can ship faster with less friction and stronger reliability at scale.
 Who We Are
 ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE’s world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world’s largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy, day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.
As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE’s near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Designed for dual use, the platform also serves civil protection and commercial users for natural-catastrophe intelligence, insurance, maritime monitoring including oil-spill detection, and finance, contributing to global security and community resilience.
ICEYE is headquartered in Finland and operates globally across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We have more than 900 employees, united by a shared vision: improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.
 Your Day-to-day Responsibilities
 Design, operate, and continuously improve a secure, scalable, and resilient Kubernetes platform across cloud and on-prem environments
 Build and maintain standardized platform capabilities such as ingress, service mesh, secrets management, and lifecycle automation
 Develop reusable infrastructure patterns and Terraform modules for AWS and on-prem platforms to enable fast, auditable provisioning
 Strengthen observability through clear metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and actionable alerting that support effective operational decisions
 Reduce platform friction for product teams by providing architectural guidance, platform standards, and hands-on enablement
 Automate platform lifecycle management including bootstrap, upgrades, scaling, and operational maintenance to reduce manual effort and risk
 Drive technical direction and sound architectural choices across platform engineering with pragmatic trade-offs between reliability, security, speed, and maintainability
 Help raise engineering maturity by mentoring others and shaping shared engineering standards across teams
 Must Haves
 What we’re looking for
 8+ years of experience in Platform Engineering, SRE, DevOps, or infrastructure roles operating production-critical services at scale
 Deep hands-on expertise with Kubernetes, including cluster architecture, upgrades, control plane operations, networking, ingress, storage, security, and lifecycle management
 Strong understanding of AWS fundamentals, including networking, IAM, compute, storage, and security patterns
 Strong experience with Terraform and infrastructure as code, including reusable modules, abstractions, and scalable provisioning patterns
 Strong practical observability experience, including SLO and SLI design, instrumentation, dashboarding, alert strategy, and production performance analysis
 Proficiency in at least one backend language such as Python or Go for automation, tooling, and internal platform capabilities
 Experience providing technical leadership through platform standards, architectural guidance, and hands-on enablement
 Ability to operate effectively in complex environments and make pragmatic technical decisions across reliability, security, speed, and maintainability
 Nice To Haves
 Experience with Rancher, Istio, External Secrets, Vault, and software supply-chain hardening practices
 Experience operating Kubernetes in restricted, disconnected, or air-gapped environments
 Experience with hybrid platforms spanning AWS and on-prem environments such as vSphere or VxRail
 Application Process
 Talent Attraction Introduction
 Hiring Manager Alignment
 Task Assignment
 Technical Interview
 Director Interview
 Working at ICEYE
 At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.
 How We Work (Our Values)
 Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.
 Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the why behind decisions.
 See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.
 Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.
 Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.
 Have fun: What we do matters and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.
 Benefits
 Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing, at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.
 Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
 We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.
We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us and we will do our best to help.
Apply now to start your ICEYE journey and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com.

Tätigkeitsbeschreibung: 
 In order to support the Test Means Component GR Team, Airbus is looking for a 
 Software Developer for Lab Test Means (d/f/m) 
 Within the Test Means & Digital platform domain, the 'Test Means Components' sub-department verifies and supports all instrumentation and test environments for laboratory, respectively ground test installations across all aircraft programs. 
 You will integrate into the new and motivated Test Means Components team (across the Hamburg and Bremen sites) and serve as the Software Developer for Lab Test Means (d/f/m), taking full responsibility for ground test means components. In this role, you will be in charge of ensuring operational availability, driving new developments, and executing lifecycle governance of test means components while strictly complying with relevant quality standards and development processes. The main focus will be on Software Development according to German needs, e.g. test bricks for Ground Test Automation (GTA), Test Management System (TMS) and the Data Access Management System (DAMS): 
 GTA: This software enables automated and remote testing. As Software Developer (d/f/m), you are responsible for developing and adapting local GTA bridges according to different test requirements based on the core GTA brick. 
 TMS: The software drives the instrumentation, distributes parameters around between all necessary computers, executes simulation models, transmitting information between each. 
 DAMS: This software tool records all test data from a test bench and uploads it to an archive. 
 You will work closely with your transnational peers to foster best practices and lessons learned for a harmonized global approach. With a focus on software, you will take over responsibility for existing applications, including their registration and maintenance in ATOM (database). 
 If you have strong experience in test instrumentation and software development, a passion for product ownership, and the motivation to manage end-to-end testing solutions in an operational aerospace environment, this job is for you! 
 Your location 
 You will be working across the Hamburg and Bremen sites. 
 You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy. 
 Bremen is a charming city full of history in the northwest of Germany. In addition to being one of the country’s greenest cities, it offers wonderful sights, a rich culture, urban flair and culinary delights. It’s also a great place for seaside lovers, being located just an hour’s drive from the North Sea coast. 
 Our Benefits for You 
 Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines. 
 Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities. 
 Growth Made Easy: Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives. 
 Feel Good at Work: On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations. 
 Diversity Connects: Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA. 
 Your tasks and responsibilities 
 Product Ownership & Strategy: Act as the Product Responsible and End-to-End (E2E) referent for catalogue solutions, managing technical relationships and performance with internal and external suppliers. 
 Test Means Components Development: Propose and/or develop innovative test means components tailored to the specific requirements of Architects and Specialists, serving as the core Product Technical Referent for the architecture team. 
 Software Development: Based on GTA, develop and adapt software bricks according to specific needs. Functional testing and cybersecurity compliance are mandatory. 
 Operational Accountability: Ensure maximum availability and optimal utilization of all test means components. This includes executing hardware (H/W) and software (S/W) qualification tests, creating and updating Technical Sheets, and overseeing infrastructure reporting and documentation. The objective is to provide a fully validated solution for test benches. 
 Lifecycle & Maintenance: Lead H/W maintenance of test means, manage S/W maintenance & evolutions, and proactively perform obsolescence monitoring and mitigation. 
 Verification & Support: Responsible for the validation and verification of performance tests. Provide comprehensive technical support for all core and add-on functions, including hands-on integration support. 
 Supply Chain & Logistics: Manage the specific supply of critical components not covered under standard logistic mini-stocks (e.g., specialized test units). 
 Process Compliance: Ensure all new component developments fully comply with relevant processes and quality metrics defined for test means. 
 Desired skills and qualifications 
 Bachelor degree in informatics or an equivalent degree programme 
 Strong background in the test instrumentation domain, avionics knowledge, ground test environments, or physical measurements. 
 Proven experience in Product Ownership, Software Development, project management, or supplier management within an engineering context. 
 Solid knowledge of hardware and software integration, maintenance lifecycles, and qualification testing. 
 Aeronautical system knowledge and familiarity with test architecture. 
 Advanced level of English (working language). 
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to manage interfaces between architects, specialists, and suppliers. 
 Agility to multitask in a highly operational and fast-paced environment. 
 Problem-solving mindset and a proactive approach to obsolescence and technical challenges. 
 Ability and interest in teamwork across transnational sites (Hamburg, Bremen, Toulouse, and UK). 
 Autonomy and adaptability to integrate innovative and emerging technologies in a ground test context. 
 Open-mindedness, curiosity, and a positive attitude. 
 Occasional travel is part of the mission. 
 Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth with customized development solutions.

About Us
 Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.
The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.
 Role Summary
 The Berlin team is looking for a Software Engineer - Connected Vehicle Platform, to design, build, and operate software connecting vehicle systems with infotainment, cloud, and mobile ecosystems. You will bridge low-level communication paths and high-level vehicle interfaces, developing reusable platform capabilities while supporting brand-specific configurations.
This role combines software development, systems integration, troubleshooting, and developer enablement. You will help turn vehicle signals and hardware capabilities into dependable services, libraries, gateway behaviors, and APIs that partner engineers can discover, integrate, test, and use successfully. The role is well suited to a developer who enjoys working across system boundaries and taking software from design through production support.
This role is based in our Berlin office and requires a minimum of three days per week onsite.
 Responsibilities
 Design, develop, test, and maintain communication services, client libraries, gateway and routing components, and deployment configurations; implement message publication and subscription, request/reply interactions, service discovery, signal routing, gateway translation, and reliable failure handling.
 Contribute to software components written in C++, Rust, Go, Kotlin, or other languages used across vehicle and cloud platform layers; evolve interface contracts, schemas, configuration models, and generated APIs while preserving compatibility for existing consumers.
 Decide whether functionality belongs in a reusable platform abstraction, gateway mapping, vehicle service, application, or vehicle- or brand-specific integration; deploy and validate services across vehicle-oriented compute platforms, virtualized embedded environments, simulators, software-in-the-loop systems, benches, and prototype vehicles.
 Investigate issues across vehicle interfaces, gateways, message-passing services, vehicle-model APIs, and consuming applications using logs, traces, packet captures, diagnostics, and test tools; improve reliability, performance, observability, security, deployment automation, and test coverage.
 Support partner developers through integration guidance, examples, troubleshooting, documentation, and technical issue triage; collaborate with hardware, firmware, embedded, cloud, infotainment, security, validation, product, and external partner teams.
 Participate in design reviews, code reviews, incident follow-up, and continuous improvement of engineering practices.
 Qualifications
 Degree in Computer Science or related field (or equivalent experience) plus 3+ years developing software in distributed systems, embedded platforms, or middleware; strong C++, Rust, Go, or Kotlin skills across a multi-language platform.
 Experience with messaging, gRPC, event-driven architectures, distributed systems, and designing or using Protobuf contracts (or equivalent), APIs, and schemas.
 Familiarity with CAN/DBC, vehicle gateways, signal integration, and connected devices; physical-input or HMI gateway experience is a plus.
 Ability to deploy and debug on embedded/virtual platforms (Android Automotive, Linux, test benches, simulators) with experience in CI/CD, Docker, or Bazel.
 Knowledge of mutual TLS, auth, telemetry (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry), and end-to-end troubleshooting using logs, traces, and packet captures.
 Strong communication skills to support developer adoption via SDKs and docs; experience with platform abstractions, automotive partners, Clean Architecture, and TDD/DDD.
 Total Rewards
 We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program.
Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incentive plans, including applicable vesting requirements.
In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. Offerings vary by country. Learn more about our global benefit programs .

About Us 
 QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.
 With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in! 
 Our Systems Integration Team is seeking a Model-Based Systems Engineer to build the tools and framework we use to design the systems that operate our VIO and QPU technology. This role is focused on establishing QuantWare’s MBSE methodology and turning knowledge from cryogenics, wiring, control electronics and software into a single, executable system model. You will define how we model our systems and build the libraries, analyses and integrations that make the model useful day to day. Working closely with processor, hardware and software teams, you will play an important role in enabling the design of the large-scale quantum computers built around VIO-powered QPUs.
 What are you going to do? 
 Define and own QuantWare’s MBSE methodology, modelling conventions and architecture framework for quantum computing systems, covering the quantum processor, cryostat, signal chain, control and readout electronics, and software stack.
 Select, set up and maintain the MBSE toolchain (e.g. SysML v2, Capella or Cameo), including version control, model reviews and integration with existing engineering tools.
 Build reusable model libraries for key subsystems, including QPU interfaces, cryogenic wiring and attenuation, microwave signal paths, and control electronics.
 Develop automated analyses on top of the model, such as heat-load, signal-integrity and noise budgets, channel counts, scalability, and full-system metrics such as power consumption as qubit counts grow.
 Establish requirements traceability from customer and system-level requirements down to component specifications and verification tests.
 Connect the system model to simulation and measurement data, creating a digital thread between design and test.
 Support system architecture and trade studies for new VIO and QPU generations and customer system integrations.

items.jobTitle: UI Engineer (Based in CA or NC only)
items.jobDescription:
Mission: Live at the intersection of app runtime & security. Protect applications in a fundamental way so that developers can build great application services and not be constantly looking over their shoulder. BlueRock is changing the landscape of App runtime security.
 The role 
 Location: Must be based in CA (preferably San Francisco Bay Area) or North Carolina 
 You will work alongside BlueRock's product designers and the control plane development team on our operator consoles. These are the React front ends that engineers and security teams use to manage large fleets of protected nodes, see what AI agents are actually doing across those fleets, and author the policy that constrains them.
 The domain is AI and agentic systems, seen from the operations and security side. When an agent calls an MCP server, spawns a subagent, runs a shell command in a sandbox, or burns $40 of tokens in an afternoon, our UI is where a person sees it, understands it, and decides what to allow. So the interesting problems are visibility problems (how do you show a thousand agent sessions so someone can find the one that matters?) and control problems (how do you author an enforcement policy without a mistake taking production down?).
 This is a mid-level role. We expect about 3–5 years of professional front-end experience, or equivalent work that clearly shows the same judgment. The ideal candidate is passionate about user experience, design, and AI-assisted software development, with a demonstrated grounding in engineering best practices. The title says UI, but the work doesn’t stop there: you’ll work closely with our backend services, and a feature is finished when it’s proven working live, not when the screen looks right.
 Working with design delivered as code 
 At BlueRock, product designers design and collaborate in code. Instead of handing off static mockups, they build working UI with AI coding tools, against real data, and open merge requests. Iteration happens so quickly that it has outpaced our capacity for robust engineering collaboration and review.
 This role closes that gap. You will collaborate directly with product designers and backend developers to keep UI development fast, by bridging the gap between vibe code and high-quality, sustainable, well-tested code. Some days that means reviewing and hardening a designer's branch so it can merge. Other days it means building the shared components, tests and guardrails that make the next branch need less hardening.
 Beyond reviewing and hardening code, you'll help shape how it gets made. Working with designers and the AI tools they use, you'll turn what each review teaches us into shared components, conventions, tests and agent instructions. Over time the whole practice becomes more predictable, and each new branch arrives closer to production-ready.
 Roles and collaboration 
 Software development roles are blurring more than ever. This role reports to product design, with API and data-layer guidance from our control plane engineering lead. You must be attuned to the perspectives of both UX/Design and Engineering, acting as a bridge between the goals and priorities of both sides, while ultimately deferring to UX/design partners on matters of style, copy, and information architecture.
 In practice: when a designer's branch makes a choice about layout, copy or flow, you protect the intent and fix the implementation. When the implementation can't support the intent, because of performance, data shape or maintainability, you say so early and bring options rather than quietly changing the design.
 What you'll do 
 Review designer-authored merge requests and bring them to production quality: structure, types, tests, accessibility, performance, and both light and dark themes.
 Turn one-off UI from fast iteration into shared, documented components in our design system and Storybook, and migrate the apps onto them.
 Make data-dense views hold up at real scale. Dashboards, tables, charts, and time-range and filter controls that work on a demo tenant also have to work on one with billions of events.
 Wire UI to the API layer (GraphQL), and work with backend developers when a view needs a new query, field or endpoint.
 Own UI test coverage: Vitest for units and Playwright for end-to-end flows, kept green in CI.
 Test UI end to end in live, secured environments, with full authentication and authorization, real data and realistic load, before calling it done.
 Keep UI work moving across release lines: shipping behind feature flags, and carrying fixes between branches when a release is frozen.
 Fix UI bugs across the consoles and the Windows, Mac and Linux clients: layout and overflow, tooltips and popovers, empty and zero states, things that are technically correct and still confusing.
 When needed, design new interfaces within the existing design system, and bring them to design for review.
 Help set the guardrails that make AI-assisted UI development safe: lint rules, conventions, review checklists, and the instructions our AI coding tools follow.
 How we expect you to work 
 These are the habits of a careful engineer. They matter more here, not less, because so much of the code you touch was drafted quickly by someone else or by an AI tool.
 Diagnose before you change. Find the actual cause, which is usually a layer away from the symptom, and be able to explain why your fix addresses it. A change that makes the symptom disappear is not the same as a fix.
 Small, deliberate diffs. Solve the problem in front of you. Don't refactor adjacent code on the way past, and don't build the abstraction you may need later.
 Fix it in one place. When the same bug shows up in three panels, the fix belongs in the shared component, not copied three times. Knowing where a change belongs is most of the skill.
 Verify, then claim. Run it, look at it, check both themes and a narrow viewport, get types and lint clean, and write the test where a test is what proves it. Then say plainly what you checked and what you did not. This applies double to AI-assisted work: you own the diff, whoever drafted it.
 Say when you're unsure. A requirement with two readings is a question, not a guess. Surfacing a problem early is always cheaper than discovering it in review.
 Our UI stack and design system 
 Our front ends are several React and TypeScript apps that share one codebase: our enterprise operator consoles and our cloud product for builders.
 All of them are built on our own design system. It is a shared React component library on top of Ant Design, with design tokens for color, type and spacing, light and dark themes, and a shared app shell for navigation, page layout and headers. Every component is documented in Storybook, published from CI, which serves as the reference for designers, engineers and AI coding tools alike. The library also carries written instructions for AI coding assistants, so generated code reaches for the system's components and tokens instead of inventing its own.
 A large part of this role is the design system itself. That means promoting patterns out of individual apps into shared components, writing their stories, keeping tokens and themes consistent so the apps don't drift, and making the system the easiest path for anyone, or any agent, building UI.
 Front end: React, TypeScript, Vite
 Design system: our component library built on Ant Design, including design tokens and light and dark themes
 Documentation: Storybook, published to GitLab Pages
 Data and charts: GraphQL; ECharts for the data-dense views
 Testing: Vitest, Playwright, and contract and smoke suites in CI
 Delivery: GitLab merge requests and pipelines, release branches, feature flags
 Further back: TypeScript and Rust services over graph and columnar stores, built on OpenTelemetry, plus desktop apps and services across Mac, Windows and Linux
 You don't need experience with all of it. You do need to be strong in TypeScript and React, and willing to read code before changing it.
 What you bring 
 About 3–5 years building production front ends in TypeScript and modern React: hooks, composition, state that lives at the right level, and an understanding of why a re-render happens.
 An end-to-end view of the systems behind the UI. Designing in code gets a feature most of the way to working, and you close the rest of the gap. For you, “done” doesn’t stop at the UI working. It means the UI is integrated and shown to work live, in a secured environment with full authentication and authorization, under realistic load.
 Integration testing against complex backends. Tests that only run against mock data in a standalone dev stack aren’t enough here. You can create, integrate and run tests in live environments to check data validity, load, security and scale, and you keep unit, integration and end-to-end suites green in CI.
 Performance instincts for data-heavy UI: pagination, virtualization, server-side filtering, and knowing when a slow page is a query problem rather than a rendering problem.
 A track record of reviewing other people’s code and improving it without rewriting it.
 Git in complex repositories with several active release branches, where a single fix may need to be cherry-picked, ported or graft-merged onto more than one of them. Readable commits, and responding to review without taking it personally.
 Hands-on use of AI coding tools in real work, with clear habits for checking what they produce.
 CSS that holds up: flexbox and grid, overflow and scroll containers, responsive behaviour, and why a tooltip or popover ends up clipped.
 Experience building or contributing to a component library or design system, ideally with Storybook and design tokens.
 Careful attention to visual detail and real interest in UX. Much of this work is noticing that something is two pixels wrong, or that a label is technically correct and still confusing.
 Genuine interest in the AI and agentic space, and in the operational and security questions it creates.
 Nice to have: Ant Design; GraphQL; ECharts or other charting libraries; design training or a portfolio; experience on a team where designers commit code; writing conventions or instructions for AI coding tools; desktop UI across Mac, Windows and Linux; dense operational tooling such as observability, security or infrastructure products.
 Not required: a computer science degree, if your work shows the same rigor. Deep backend, security or infrastructure expertise, or any knowledge of our domain (fleet management, telemetry, agent observability, policy enforcement). We will teach that.
 Your first 90 days 
 First month: land changes safely. Ship scoped fixes in the consoles. Learn the component library, theme tokens and API layer. Start reviewing designer merge requests alongside an engineer.
 Second month: own review on a surface. Become the primary reviewer for designer-authored UI on one product area, and extract at least one repeated pattern into a shared component.
 Third month: make the next branch easier. Get the flows you own covered by tests in CI, and write down the conventions and guardrails that make designer branches need less hardening.
 About BlueRock: 
 BlueRock is a well-funded, early stage cybersecurity company founded by experienced security minded entrepreneurs. Our mission is to change the game in cybersecurity. Attackers are exploiting in hours. The dependency tree is exploding. Developers are drowning in vulnerability debt. BlueRock changes the game, enabling organizations to shift from chasing CVEs and exploits to proactively protecting the foundations of applications and computing, so that developers can build great applications without looking over their shoulders.

About the Job
 We are looking for a Control Engineer (m/f/d) to bring locomotion control to our robot, from simulation to real hardware. You will own the full path from model to motor: identify the dynamics, design controllers, train reinforcement learning policies and make them run reliably on the real robot. The work spans simulation, real-time control and firmware. It has to hold up against model errors, sensor noise, latency and hardware that does not behave like the simulator.
 Responsibilities
 Locomotion Control: Design, implement and tune controllers for a robot, from joint-level torque and impedance control up to whole-body and locomotion control.
 Real-Time & Firmware Integration: Integrate controllers and policies into the real-time control stack and work on the firmware side (motor drivers, communication buses, safety limits) together with the hardware team.
 RL Policy Training: Train locomotion policies in simulation (e.g. Isaac Lab, MuJoCo), including reward design, curricula and domain randomization.
 Sim2Real Transfer: Deploy trained policies on the real robot and close the sim2real gap through actuator, latency and noise modeling and systematic hardware experiments.
 System Identification: Identify actuator and rigid-body dynamics (inertia, friction, motor models) from robot data and feed the results back into simulation and controllers.
 Testing & Validation: Build test setups and benchmarks in simulation and on hardware, and run reliability checks before demos and releases.
 Documentation: Document models, controllers and procedures so others can reproduce and extend them.
 Essential Skills
 Engineering Background: Degree in Robotics, Control Engineering, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science or a related field, or an equivalent qualification plus professional experience with comparable systems.
 Robot Dynamics & Control: Solid foundation in rigid-body dynamics and feedback control (e.g. torque/impedance control, MPC, whole-body control), applied on physical robots.
 Reinforcement Learning: Hands-on experience training RL policies for robot control in simulation (e.g. PPO with Isaac Lab or MuJoCo).
 Sim2Real: Experience transferring controllers or learned policies from simulation to real hardware and debugging the gap.
 C++ and Python: Professional experience writing C++ for real-time robot control on embedded targets, and Python for training, analysis and tooling.
 Hands-on Hardware Debugging: Comfortable working directly on real robots, reading logs and signals, and tracking problems across software, electronics and mechanics.
 Beneficial Skills
 Legged Robots: Experience with quadrupeds or humanoids, in locomotion or whole-body control.
 System Identification: Experience identifying robot or actuator dynamics (excitation trajectories, physically consistent parameter estimation, friction models).
 Firmware & Embedded: Experience with embedded C/C++, motor control (FOC), real-time systems (e.g. PREEMPT_RT, Xenomai) or field buses such as EtherCAT or CAN.
 ROS 2 & Middleware: Experience with ROS 2, ros2_control or DDS.
 Simulation Modeling: Experience building or tuning robot models in MuJoCo or Isaac Sim.
 Infrastructure: Docker, CI pipelines and GPU training setups.

 A dynamic high-tech company, combined with financial soundness and world-class investors. 
 Join an interdisciplinary, international team with 60+ different nationalities in a collaborative work environment. 
 Lots of development opportunities as we continue to grow. 
 Challenging tasks and impactful projects alongside experts that enable professional and personal growth.

 Agile Robots is a leading provider of AI-powered robotics solutions. By combining artificial intelligence and robotics, the company makes industries smarter, more flexible, and more efficient. 
 Founded in Munich in 2018 by renowned robotics researchers from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Agile Robots has experienced rapid global growth. Today, more than 3,500 highly skilled robotics and AI enthusiasts are employed worldwide. The company has one of the largest research and development teams in the AI and robotics industry.

items.jobTitle: PhD Position (w/m/d) in datengetriebener Simulation und digitalen Zwillingen
items.jobDescription:
In der Forschungsgruppe Systems, Data, Simulation & Energy (SYDSEN) am Institut AIFB, geleitet von Prof. Sanja Lazarova-Molnar, ist eine Doktorandenstelle zu besetzen.
Wir entwickeln neue Methoden der datengetriebenen Modellierung und Simulation zur Weiterentwicklung digitaler Zwillinge, unter anderem mit Anwendungen in Energie- und Fertigungssystemen. Dabei verbinden wir Betriebsdaten, Simulationsmodelle und Expertenwissen, um die automatisierte Modellerstellung und -anpassung, Zuverlässigkeitsbewertung und Entscheidungsfindung zu unterstützen.
Unsere Forschung umfasst nationale und internationale Verbundprojekte, darunter die europäischen Forschungsprojekte ONE4ALL und DMaaST . Die Forschungsarbeiten im Rahmen der Promotion orientieren sich an den wissenschaftlichen Schwerpunkten der Forschungsgruppe und können an laufende Arbeiten im Zusammenhang mit diesen Projekten anknüpfen.
 Ihre Aufgaben
 Ihre Aufgaben
 Wissenschaftliche Forschung im Bereich datengetriebene Modellierung, Simulation und Digitale Zwillinge sowie Entwicklung und Evaluation neuer Methoden.
 Bearbeitung wissenschaftlicher Fragestellungen innerhalb der Forschungsschwerpunkte der Gruppe und Veröffentlichung der Ergebnisse in renommierten Fachzeitschriften und auf internationalen Konferenzen.
 Aktive Mitarbeit in nationalen und internationalen Forschungsprojekten und Kooperationen.
 Aktive Mitwirkung in der Lehre sowie bei der Betreuung studentischer Projekte und Abschlussarbeiten.
 Mitwirkung bei der Entwicklung neuer Forschungsideen und der Erstellung von Drittmittelanträgen.
 Übernahme organisatorischer und administrativer Aufgaben im Rahmen der Forschungsgruppe sowie des Lehr- und Forschungsbetriebs.
 Ihr Profil
 Sehr guter Hochschulabschluss (Master) in Informatik oder einem eng verwandten Fach mit fundierten Informatikkenntnissen.
 Gute Kenntnisse in Algorithmen, Mathematik und zentralen Grundlagen der Informatik sowie solide Programmierkenntnisse.
 Interesse an Modellierung und Simulation, datengetriebenen Methoden und digitalen Zwillingen.
 Wissenschaftliche Neugier, kritisches Denken, Eigeninitiative und Motivation zur Entwicklung neuer Forschungsmethoden.
 Bereitschaft, sich in neue wissenschaftliche Fragestellungen einzuarbeiten und aktiv zu den Forschungsaktivitäten der Gruppe beizutragen.
 Gute Deutschkenntnisse oder die Bereitschaft, Deutsch zu lernen (Lehraufgaben können Deutschkenntnisse erfordern).
 Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse.
 Wir bieten
 Forschung mit Wirkung : Arbeiten Sie an Themen von gesellschaftlicher Relevanz – in einem exzellenten wissenschaftlichen Umfeld, das Veränderungen möglich macht. 
 Karriere und Entwicklung : Wir unterstützen Sie mit einer strukturierten Einarbeitung, vielfältigen Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten und individueller Förderung. So stärken wir Ihr persönliches Wachstum. 
 Flexible Arbeitszeitgestaltung : Nutzen Sie Gleitzeit, mobiles Arbeiten und 30 Tage Urlaub für eine optimale Work-Life-Balance. 
 Familienfreundlichkeit : Das Programm „KIT-Family +“ unterstützt Sie bei der Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf – durch Kinderbetreuung, Ferienangebote, ein Eltern-Kind-Büro und Hilfe bei der Angehörigenpflege. 
 Gesundheit : Unter dem Motto „Fit im KIT – mit Körper, Geist und Seele“ fördern wir Ihre Gesundheit mit Sportkursen und Angeboten zur psychischen Gesundheit. 
 Individuelle Zusatzleistungen : Profitieren Sie von einer betrieblichen Altersvorsorge (VBL), einem monatlichen Zuschuss von 25 Euro zum Jobticket BW sowie vielfältigen Angeboten rund um Kultur und Freizeit. 
 Arbeitsort 
 Karlsruhe (und Eggenstein-Leopoldshafen)
 Eingruppierung
 EG 13 TV-L; die Eingruppierung erfolgt entsprechend den persönlichen und fachlichen Voraussetzungen.
 Vertragsdauer
 4 Jahre
 Fachliche Auskünfte erhalten Sie von
 Prof. Dr.-Ing. Sanja Lazarova-Molnar
lazarova-molnar@kit.edu
 Bei allgemeinen Fragen zur Bewerbung wenden Sie sich bitte an
 Julia Boldt
Personalservice (PSE)
julia.boldt@partner.kit.edu
Bitte laden Sie die folgenden Unterlagen als eine einzige PDF-Datei hoch: ein Motivationsschreiben (maximal eine Seite), in dem Sie Ihre Forschungsinteressen, relevante Forschungserfahrungen und Ihre Motivation für eine Promotion in unserer Forschungsgruppe erläutern; Ihren Lebenslauf; Notenübersichten aus dem Bachelor- und Masterstudium; eine Kopie Ihrer Masterarbeit (ein Entwurf ist ausreichend) sowie die Namen und Kontaktdaten von zwei akademischen Referenzpersonen. Bitte geben Sie Ihren Namen im Dateinamen an.

Über YLAB
 Wir bauen die KI, die wir unseren eigenen Kindern geben würden.
 Kinder wachsen heute mit KI auf. Wir sorgen dafür, dass diese KI neugierig macht statt süchtig, sicher ist statt datenhungrig und für Kinder gebaut wird statt für Erwachsene.
 Wir sind YLAB, ein kleines KI-Lab aus Köln-Ehrenfeld. Wir entwickeln Software und Hardware aus einer Hand, vom Sprachmodell bis zum Gehäuse. Unser erstes Produkt ist Onoo, ein Lernbegleiter ohne Bildschirm für Kinder ab vier. Onoo fragt zurück, lässt raten und denkt mit. Er hat keine Kamera und kein Display, zeigt keine Werbung und verkauft keine Daten.
 Warum YLAB
 Deine Arbeit landet im Kinderzimmer, nicht in einem Dashboard.
 Software & Hardware: KI, App, Firmware und Gerät entstehen bei uns zusammen. Du siehst, wie aus Code etwas wird, das ein Kind in die Hand nimmt.
 Du arbeitest an echten offenen Fragen, zum Beispiel wie KI Kinderstimmen versteht und Fünfjährigen die Welt erklärt.
 Tech, Pädagogik und Forschung sitzen bei uns an einem Tisch.
 Ehrlichkeit statt Hochglanz: Vieles bauen wir zum ersten Mal. Wenn dich das reizt, sollten wir reden.
 Was wir bieten
 Verantwortung ab Tag eins: Du bekommst echte Themen und Probleme statt Tickets, und deine Entscheidungen haben Gewicht.
 Top Arbeitsmaterial: Du arbeitest mit dem Setup und den Tools, die du brauchst.
 Flexible Weiterbildung: Konferenz, Kurs oder Workshop – du sagst uns, was dich weiterbringt.
 Hybrid mit Herz: Remote, wenn du Ruhe brauchst, und im Office, wenn wir gemeinsam tüfteln.
 Über die Rolle
 Onoo hört zu, denkt mit und antwortet kindgerecht. Dahinter stecken Spracherkennung, ein kuratierter Wissensraum und eine mehrstufige Safety-Pipeline. Der Prototyp funktioniert, der Launch ist 2027. Jetzt bauen wir die Pipeline, die Millionen Kinderfragen aushält.
 Du bist unsere erste dedizierte AI/ML-Stelle, mit Platz am Gründertisch. Du arbeitest direkt mit Lennard (CEO, Product & AI) und entscheidest mit, wie unser Stack aussieht. Vom Modell-Routing bis zum Latenzbudget auf dem Gerät.
 Was dich erwartet: echte Edge-Cases wie Kinderstimmen, Dialekte und Quatschfragen, dazu harte Grenzen bei Latenz, Kosten und Datenschutz. Und die Verantwortung, dass jede Antwort sicher ist, bevor sie ein Kind erreicht.
 Wie du uns helfen kannst
 Du baust und betreibst unsere Sprach-Pipeline: Spracherkennung für Kinderstimmen, Dialogführung, Sprachausgabe. Schnell genug fürs Wohnzimmer.
 Du orchestrierst Sprachmodelle provider-agnostisch: Routing, Prompting, Evals, Kostenkontrolle.
 Du entwickelst unsere Safety-Layer weiter: Klassifikatoren, Guardrails, mehrstufige Prüfungen vor jeder Antwort.
 Du baust Evaluations-Sets aus echten Kinderfragen und misst, was „gut erklärt“ heißt.
 Du bringst Modelle in Produktion: EU-Hosting, Monitoring, Fallbacks, saubere Degradation.
 Du arbeitest eng mit Research und Pädagogik, damit Erkenntnisse im Produkt landen.
 Du hältst unseren Stack einfach. Lieber ein robuster Pfad als fünf halbe.
 Melde dich, wenn:
 Du hast 3+ Jahre ML/AI in Produktion gebracht, nicht nur in Notebooks.
 Du kennst dich mit LLM-Pipelines aus: Prompting, RAG, Evals, Latenz- und Kosten-Tuning.
 Audio/Speech (ASR/TTS) ist für dich kein Neuland. Oder du hast Lust, dich reinzubeißen.
 Python ist dein Zuhause und TypeScript schreckt dich nicht.
 Du triffst lieber Entscheidungen, als auf fertige Specs zu warten.
 Datenschutz und Safety sind für dich Teil des Designs, keine Checkliste.
 Du willst, dass deine Arbeit im Kinderzimmer ankommt und nicht im Backlog.
 Eher nicht, wenn: du nur Modelle trainieren willst und Produktion dich langweilt. Oder wenn du erst loslegst, wenn Anforderungen, Team und Prozesse fertig sind.

About Us
 Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally.  
 Data Engineer III 
 About the Role 
We're looking for a Data Engineer III to join our Data Engineering team, which builds and governs the data foundation that powers the business. You'll work within our stack — Python ingestion pipelines, Airflow orchestration, and Snowflake/Databricks — helping move data reliably and securely from source to decision-ready output.
You'll implement features and fixes against a given design, handle known classes of pipeline issues on your own, and escalate genuinely novel problems with clear context rather than working them in isolation. You're also expected to start contributing meaningfully in code review — catching real bugs, not just style nits.
 What You'll Do 
 Implement new ingestion sources end-to-end against a senior engineer's design — connector code, DAG, schema, monitoring, and catalog registration — extending the team's existing framework where a new source needs a pattern it doesn't yet support
 Investigate pipeline failures independently, recognize known classes of issues, and ship the documented fix without needing to escalate
 Before shipping a new pipeline, identify downstream consumers and what would break if data were late or wrong, and flag gaps like this during spec review — before writing code
 Write clear handovers when escalating a genuinely unresolved issue — what you tried, what you ruled out, and where things diverge — so a senior can pick up without re-discovery
 Review peers' pipeline PRs and catch non-obvious issues (e.g., missing idempotency checks, race conditions) that could cause incorrect downstream data
 Turn ambiguous "why is this data wrong?" questions into structured investigations — tracing data lineage from source to warehouse and communicating back what you found
 Surface concerns in spec review as specific, well-reasoned questions rather than staying silent or blocking progress
 Support data security and governance work (e.g., PII masking, access controls) and contribute to data delivery work, including reverse ETL integrations
 Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders and help scope and clarify requirements for new work
 Mentor DE2s on their first significant projects — pairing on tricky decisions and helping them apply team conventions
 What We're Looking For 
 3–5 years of professional software or data engineering experience
 Strong SQL and Python skills, with solid experience building and operating production data pipelines
 Comfort investigating and root-causing pipeline issues independently before escalating
 Experience with workflow orchestration tools (Airflow or similar) and a cloud data warehouse/lakehouse (Snowflake, Databricks, or similar)
 Solid understanding of data pipeline concepts: idempotency, schema evolution, backfills, and data quality/testing
 Experience giving substantive code review feedback, not just style or formatting comments
 Strong communication skills — can write a clear technical handover, ask sharp questions in spec review, and explain a data lineage investigation to a non-technical stakeholder
 A track record of taking ownership of known-class problems end-to-end rather than needing step-by-step direction
 Nice to Have 
 Experience extending or building reusable pipeline frameworks/templates
 Exposure to reverse ETL tools or patterns, PII masking, or data access governance (RBAC)
 Exposure to observability/monitoring tooling (e.g., Datadog) for pipeline health and alerting
 Some experience mentoring or informally supporting more junior engineers
 Background in gaming, betting, e-commerce, or another regulated/high-compliance industry
 Why Join Us 
 Real ownership over known-class problems, with senior/staff support available for the genuinely novel ones
 Work on high-visibility, high-trust systems that the business depends on
 A culture built around clear tenets: standardize before you scale, own the outcome (not just the ticket), and clarity over complexity
 Clear growth path into Senior Data Engineer, with room to start mentoring and shaping team practices along the way

À propos de nous
 Le Groupe EMITECH, laboratoire d'essais en environnement, ingénierie, formation et conception de bancs de tests est leader dans son domaine avec 77 millions d'Euros de chiffre d'affaires, 19 sites et 700 collaborateurs.
Le Groupe, composé de plusieurs sociétés, accompagne les grands donneurs d'ordre et les PME de l'aéronautique, l'automobile, le militaire, le spatial, le ferroviaire, le médical, les télécoms dans le développement, la validation, la qualification et la certification de leurs produits (mécanique, vibratoire, climatique, radiofréquence, compatibilité électromagnétique, électrique, hydraulique...). Depuis plus de 30 ans, le Groupe EMITECH poursuit sa croissance grâce aux équipes qui le compose.
Vous avez du talent ? Vous souhaitez travaillez dans un esprit de convivialité et monter en compétences ? Nous avons un poste pour vous !
 Mission
 Au sein de notre filiale EMC et dans le cadre d'un projet client automobile, vous intervenez en qualité de metteur au point des calibrations BMS H/F.
 Vos Principales Missions Sont
 Calibration et mise au point BMS
 Réaliser les activités de calibration des fonctions BMS.
Participer à la mise au point des fonctions de surveillance des tensions et températures des cellules.
Intervenir sur les fonctions de gestion et d'estimation de l'état de charge (SOC/BSOC) et de l'état de santé (SOH).
Participer à la calibration des fonctions DCR, EOC et Quick Charge.
Contribuer à la mise au point des stratégies Multistep et NoGO Back.
Intervenir sur les fonctions de surveillance thermique : Hotspots, CellTab et Tspread.
Participer à la calibration des stratégies de limitation de puissance (Derating).
 Essais et validation
 Préparer et suivre les campagnes d'essais de validation BMS.
Participer aux essais sur banc et/ou véhicule selon les besoins du projet.
Analyser les résultats d'essais et identifier les écarts de performance.
Vérifier le bon fonctionnement des fonctions et stratégies calibrées.
Participer à la validation des diagnostics, notamment FID et IRDD.
Assurer le suivi des évolutions et des corrections de calibration.
 Analyse et reporting
 Exploiter les données issues des campagnes d'essais.
Rédiger les fiches d'essais et les rapports de validation.
Préparer les synthèses techniques aux différents jalons projet.
Assurer la traçabilité des calibrations et des résultats.
Participer à la capitalisation technique et au respect des méthodologies métier.
 Profil
 Issu(e) d’une formation BAC+2 à BAC+5 ou d’une école d’ingénieur en génie électrotechnique / génie électrique, vous disposez d’une solide connaissance des systèmes BMS et des batteries Lithium.
Vous maîtrisez les principes de calibration et de validation des systèmes embarqués.
Vous avez de bonnes connaissances des fonctions SOC, SOH, DCR ainsi que des stratégies de charge.
Vous maîtrisez les stratégies de gestion thermique et de limitation de puissance des batteries.
Vous justifiez d’une expérience significative en essais et analyse de données sur systèmes électrifiés.
Vous maîtrisez les outils de calibration et d’acquisition de données utilisés dans le secteur automobile.
 Pourquoi rejoindre le Groupe EMITECH ?
 Parce que nous sommes convaincus que nos collaborateurs sont la première richesse du Groupe EMITECH, nous mettons tout en œuvre pour les accompagner, les fidéliser et les faire grandir. Nous proposons un environnement de travail stimulant, des perspectives d'évolution, une rémunération attractive ainsi que de nombreux avantages.
 Conditions de travail : Un parcours d'intégration structuré, horaires flexibles et télétravail (selon le poste et les priorités de service).
 Convivialité : Découverte des métiers de vos collègues, challenges internes, événements familles, barbecues, repas de Noël…
 Santé & bien-être : Une mutuelle avantageuse pour vous et votre famille, avec une surcomplémentaire facultative.
 Rémunération & avantages : Rémunération attractive , prime d'intéressement, prime de cooptation, prime vacances.
 Restauration : Des titres-restaurant d’une valeur de 11,50 € pris en charge à 60 % par l'employeur.
 Épargne salariale : Un plan d'Épargne Entreprise (PEE) et Plan d'Épargne Retraite (PER).
 Développement des compétences : Formations tout le long de votre parcours.
 Avantages CSE : Des chèques vacances, bons de Noël, bons naissance, subventions cinéma et bien d'autres avantages.
 Mobilité : Un e prise en charge à 50 % de votre abonnement aux transports en commun.
 Vous souhaitez découvrir le monde des essais et évoluer dans un environnement technique, innovant et stimulant ? Vous avez envie de développer vos compétences au sein d'équipes passionnées, dans une ambiance conviviale et bienveillante ?
 Rejoignez le Groupe EMITECH et participez à une aventure humaine et technologique où votre talent fera la différence.
 Postulez dès maintenant !
