Die Bergische Universität Wuppertal ist eine dynamische, forschungsorientierte Campusuniversität. Getreu ihres Leitmotivs „Verstehen, Vermitteln, Gestalten“ widmet sie sich den großen gesellschaftlichen Herausforderungen in Wissenschaft, Bildung, Kultur, Wirtschaft, Gesellschaft, Technik und Umwelt. Sie ist aktive Partnerin in den Netzwerken der Region sowie in nationalen und internationalen Kooperationen. Rund 24.500 Menschen studieren, forschen und arbeiten hier an neun Fakultäten, in teils interdisziplinären Forschungseinrichtungen oder in der Verwaltung. 
In der Fakultät für Elektrotechnik, Informationstechnik und Medientechnik, am Lehrstuhl für Theoretische Elektrotechnik, suchen wir Unterstützung.

- Leitung eines Drittmittelprojekts
- Planung, Fortschrittskontrolle und Budgetverantwortung der Arbeitspakete im Projekt
- Ansprechperson für Industriepartner und Fördergeber
- Mentoring und Anleitung von wissenschaftlichen und fachlichen Mitarbeiter\*innen
- Interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit im Verbund (Hochschule + Industrie)
- Bearbeitung eines Arbeitspakets zu KI-gestützter Objekterkennung
- Entwicklung und Anwendung von KI-Modellen zur robusten Objekterkennung in komplexen Sensordatenszenarien
- Entwicklung adaptiver Verfahren für wechselnde Umgebungs- und Störbedingungen
- Aufbau von Datengrundlagen aus Simulation und Messung für Modelltraining und
-validierung
- Wissenschaftliche Aufbereitung und Veröffentlichung der Ergebnisse
## IHR PROFIL
- Abgeschlossenes Studium (Diplom/Magister/Master/Staatsexamen) in Elektrotechnik, Physik, Informatik oder vergleichbar; abgeschlossene Promotion wünschenswert
- Fundierte Erfahrung in KI/ML (neuronale Netze, klassische ML-Methoden)
- Grundkenntnisse in Signalverarbeitung
- Grundkenntnisse in CST Microwave Studio
- Erfahrung in der wissenschaftlichen Publikation
- Grundkenntnisse in der Leitung und Koordination von Projektarbeitspaketen
- Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Industriepartnern und Fördergebern
- Teamfähigkeit, Moderationsfähigkeit, Kommunikationsstärke
- Hohes Maß an Eigenverantwortung und Entscheidungsfreude
- Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse (Level C1)
- Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse von Vorteil
- Verlässlichkeit sowie ein ausgeprägtes Problem- und Risikobewusstsein im Bereich der IT- und Datensicherheit
- Bereitschaft zu wissenschaftlichem Austausch, Konferenzen und externer Vortragstätigkeit

26328

Über YLAB
 Wir bauen die KI, die wir unseren eigenen Kindern geben würden.
 Kinder wachsen heute mit KI auf. Wir sorgen dafür, dass diese KI neugierig macht statt süchtig, sicher ist statt datenhungrig und für Kinder gebaut wird statt für Erwachsene.
 Wir sind YLAB, ein kleines KI-Lab aus Köln-Ehrenfeld. Wir entwickeln Software und Hardware aus einer Hand, vom Sprachmodell bis zum Gehäuse. Unser erstes Produkt ist Onoo, ein Lernbegleiter ohne Bildschirm für Kinder ab vier. Onoo fragt zurück, lässt raten und denkt mit. Er hat keine Kamera und kein Display, zeigt keine Werbung und verkauft keine Daten.
 Warum YLAB
 Deine Arbeit landet im Kinderzimmer, nicht in einem Dashboard.
 Software & Hardware: KI, App, Firmware und Gerät entstehen bei uns zusammen. Du siehst, wie aus Code etwas wird, das ein Kind in die Hand nimmt.
 Du arbeitest an echten offenen Fragen, zum Beispiel wie KI Kinderstimmen versteht und Fünfjährigen die Welt erklärt.
 Tech, Pädagogik und Forschung sitzen bei uns an einem Tisch.
 Ehrlichkeit statt Hochglanz: Vieles bauen wir zum ersten Mal. Wenn dich das reizt, sollten wir reden.
 Was wir bieten
 Verantwortung ab Tag eins: Du bekommst echte Themen und Probleme statt Tickets, und deine Entscheidungen haben Gewicht.
 Top Arbeitsmaterial: Du arbeitest mit dem Setup und den Tools, die du brauchst.
 Flexible Weiterbildung: Konferenz, Kurs oder Workshop – du sagst uns, was dich weiterbringt.
 Hybrid mit Herz: Remote, wenn du Ruhe brauchst, und im Office, wenn wir gemeinsam tüfteln.
 Über die Rolle
 Wie versteht ein Sprachmodell eine Vierjährige? Und wie erklärt es ihr die Welt, ohne sie zu überfordern? Dazu gibt es kaum Paper und keine Benchmarks. Genau da setzt du an.
 Du bist unsere erste dedizierte Research-Stelle. Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von KI, Sprache und Pädagogik, mit echten Familien statt Laborbedingungen und mit direktem Draht ins Produkt.
 Was dich erwartet: offene Fragen mit Substanz, ein Fachbeirat aus Bildung und Psychologie und die Freiheit, Studien so zu bauen, wie sie sein müssen.
 Wie du uns helfen kannst
 Du entwirfst und machst Studien mit Kindern und Familien. Von der Beobachtung im Wohnzimmer bis zum strukturierten Test.
 Du baust Methoden, um altersgerechte Antworten zu bewerten: Was heißt verständlich, was heißt zu viel?
 Du übersetzt Erkenntnisse in Modell- und Produktentscheidungen, zusammen mit Engineering und Pädagogik.
 Du behältst die Forschung im Blick (Child-Computer Interaction, Speech, LLM-Evals) und holst rein, was uns weiterbringt.
 Du teilst, was wir lernen. Wir forschen nicht für die Schublade.
 Melde dich, wenn:
 Du hast einen Research-Hintergrund, etwa HCI, Psychologie, Linguistik oder ML.
 Du hast schon mit Nutzer:innen geforscht, am besten mit Kindern.
 Du kannst beides: Interviews auswerten und saubere Metriken bauen.
 Du schreibst klar. Für Paper genauso wie für Produktentscheidungen.
 Du magst es, wenn deine Forschung nächste Woche im Prototyp steckt.
 Eher nicht, wenn: du Forschung als Selbstzweck siehst oder zwei Jahre Vorlauf brauchst, bevor etwas testbar ist.

 Dcubed is a fast-growing space engineering company with the mission to make space engineering and exploration easy and accessible. What makes Dcubed special is that each of us is a space explorer at heart. 
 At Dcubed, we enable the future of space missions with high-performance, flight-proven release mechanisms and deployable structures.  As our AIT & Test Infrastructure Engineer - Solar Arrays (f/m/d) you will own the practical execution of hardware verification and validation activities from breadboard to flight demonstrator by developing test setups, integrating hardware, designing GSE, executing campaigns, and driving rapid learning cycles through hands-on experimentation.

Our Mission
 At Circus (Xetra: CA1), headquartered in Munich, we are pioneering global developments in on-demand autonomous food production. Everything from creation to production and operation – enabled by seamlessly integrated cutting-edge robotics and transformative AI technology.
Our foundation rests in the extensive developments of groundbreaking robotics driven by artificial intelligence, previously the missing link in achieving true autonomous food automation. This is the moment for a new status quo: Just as autonomous driving will disrupt how we build cities, organize our days, and live our lives, so will we shift our whole reality around food.
Our Team is backing a paradigm shift in one of humanity’s most important sectors with the sharpest minds in Robotics, AI, Engineering and Culinary, collaborating closely with industry-leading partners to revolutionize every aspect of the food service experience.
Join us as we forge ahead, crafting a future where the art of cooking and the science of technology converge to create a world that thinks differently about food than it has for thousands of years – a world where food means something new.
 About The Role
 Design the mechanical modules of the next generations of our robotic kitchens and take them from first sketch to serial production. You will own entire modules and subsystems, from concept through prototyping and validation to release, and see your designs run in real commercial kitchens. You will work across Robotics, Electrical, Software, Culinary and Operations, and help shape how we engineer as we move from innovation to commercial scale.
 Your Daily Business
 Own one or more modules end to end, from early concepts and prototypes through validation and release.
 Design, test and release mechanical components and subsystems for our robotic kitchen.
 Drive DFM with suppliers and partners and manage the industrialization of your parts and assemblies.
 Work with Robotics, Electrical, Culinary, Production and Operations to deliver robust designs that scale.
 Improve existing modules for performance, manufacturability and cost.
 Write technical documentation, test plans and risk assessments, including FMEA and operability analysis.
 Help define our internal engineering standards and development processes.
 Base Qualifications
 A Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
 2–5 years designing mechanical systems and assemblies for complex mechatronic products, ideally for serial production.
 Strong parametric CAD skills (SolidWorks preferred) and the ability to produce manufacturing-ready technical drawings.
 Hands-on knowledge of manufacturing processes such as sheet metal, welding, 3D printing, injection molding and casting.
 A proven track record in prototyping, testing and validating mechanical systems, in both product innovation and production scaling.
 An AI-native way of working: AI tools are a natural part of your daily work, from exploring design concepts and running analyses to writing documentation.
 Familiarity with relevant norms, compliance standards and safety/risk analysis.
 A structured, solution-driven and entrepreneurial way of working, plus excellent English.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience with flow simulation and optimization of HVLS fans, axial fans, coolers, exhausts and air circulators.
 Experience in food-tech or commercial hardware.
 Kinematic design experience.
 German language skills.
 Our Offer
 Competitive Compensation: Competitive compensation package with stock option opportunities for full-time employees.
 Work-Life Balance: Regular team events, hybrid work setup, 2 months/year remote work (Worcation), unlimited vacation days, and a corporate pension plan.
 Personal Development: Personal budget for training, in-house trainings, and growth opportunities in a fast-paced environment.
 Mobility: Monthly budget for mobility or other expenses, a subsidized Dance Mobility Subscription for E-Bike/E-Moped, and bike leasing via JobRad.

 As part of the FUTRUE Group, we have strong financial resources and a proven track record – from the first medical device for irritable bowel syndrome to the first opioid substitute for chronic pain. We turn scientific vision into clinical reality.
 We collaborate with leading research institutions worldwide and publish our results in the most prestigious international journals, including Nature and The Lancet.
 Today, FUTRUE is one of the fastest-growing healthcare companies in the world. To advance and further expand our new venture, we are looking for outstanding talents to support us in our mission.

At Alpine Eagle, we’re building the future of counter-drone defence. We’re a fast-growing, international deep-tech company working at the intersection of aerospace engineering, defence systems, and machine learning. Our goal: create the world’s first swarm-based, airborne counter-drone system.
Modern conflicts show how quickly drones are reshaping the battlefield. Threats are rising, and today’s solutions aren’t keeping pace. We’re here to change that.
Alpine Eagle isn’t just a defence company. It’s a mission. Backed by an international team, strong funding, and a bold vision, we’re looking for people who want to shape the next generation of aerial security and build something that truly matters.
🎯 How you will make an impact:
 As a Radar Software Engineer, you will be crucial in advancing our drone technology. You will develop, optimize and benchmark algorithms to further improve our radar perception with a multidisciplinary team to deliver next-generation drone solutions.
 Design, Optimize and Benchmark Algorithms: Radar processing algorithms for drone-based applications such as raw signal processing and real-time object tracking. 
 Implement and Optimize Target Platform: Implement selected algorithms for the target platform and optimize them for runtime and memory footprint. 
 Integration with Hardware: Partner with the hardware team to ensure seamless integration of computer vision models with drone systems. 
 Stay Updated: Keep abreast of the latest advancements in radar technology and signal processing for aerial and ground-based applications. 
 Code Reviews and Documentation: Participate in code reviews, maintain thorough documentation, and contribute to team discussions. 
 ✅ What you need to be successful:
 Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. PhD is a plus. 
 Strong background in Radar Signal Processing (signal processing of radar raw data, radar object tracking) with 7+ years of experience. 
 Experience in embedded SW development (ARM / Neon, Cuda) 
 Strong proficiency in C++. 
 Solid Python skills.
 Proven experience with ROS2. 
 A hands-on attitude and strong sense of ownership. 
 You approach complex problems systematically and document your results. 
 Background in radar detection KPIs and KPI driven development.
 What sets you apart from others :
 Experience with AESA radars. 
 Background in data analysis. 
 FPGA development background. 
 Experience with machine learning / AI in radar processing. 
 At Alpine Eagle, we are committed to diversity and equal opportunity. We welcome applications from all individuals regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion, disability, age, or sexual identity.
Apply now!

Why this role is exciting 
 Rohlik is the leading Central European e-grocer. More than a million customers buy their groceries from us through Rohlik.cz , Knuspr.de , Kifli.hu , Gurkerl.at and Sezamo.ro , choosing from over 17,000 items, delivered within a couple of hours in 15-minute windows.
 We are building the autonomous grocer. Maia, our AI assistant, already talks to customers and builds their orders; agents are moving into our buying and logistics; vision models are learning to watch quality. The next frontier is physical: robots taking over more and more of the work in our fulfilment centres, until fresh food moves from producers to households at a cost nobody else can match.
 We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies. Our warehouses already log what happened on every pick and every quality check, so the recordings can carry labels most datasets never get. Making that hold is part of the job.
 You decide what makes an hour of footage trainable — before we bank hundreds of them. 
 What you will own and deliver 
 The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong.
 Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap.
 The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows.
 The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations.
 Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after.
 The scope 
 This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. This is not a research-scientist role, and no publication record is required. The job is to make a corpus trainable and to train the first policies on it.
 What we are looking for 
 3+ years of relevant full-time robotics experience.
 PyTorch, and computer vision with real 3D geometry. Camera calibration, pose estimation, SLAM fundamentals. You have debugged an extrinsic calibration at least once in your life and know why it drifted.
 You can read a paper and reproduce it. Our pipeline is assembled from published work, and your job is knowing which claims survive contact with a chilled warehouse hall.
 You know what policies train on. Familiar with the current robot-learning stack and policy classes well enough to know what the training side will demand of the data before the data exists.
 Dataset instincts. You have trained on data you collected yourself, and you know the failure modes that only show up at training tim..
 Comfortable as the only ML voice. You make the call, write it down, and revisit it when the pilot data says otherwise.
 AI is how work gets done here. Our engineers use Claude Code and Devin daily, and we expect you to direct agents for the unglamorous parts — harness code, data plumbing, reproduction scripts — while keeping the quality bar exactly where it was.
 Particularly relevant. Hand-pose estimation or egocentric video in production; multi-camera rigs and time sync; experience post-training robot-learning models; ROS 2.
 What success looks like in 90 days 
 You have written the capture spec and we set up the first rigs against it. Your pilot gates have numbers, the first hours have passed your harness, and you can tell the people who sign the budget, with data, what the next hundred hours should look like.
 Are we a good fit? 
 Take this role if you would rather own the spec that decides whether a dataset becomes an asset or a write-off than tune someone else's model on someone else's data, if a fulfilment centre at 6 a.m. sounds like a lab to you, and if you want the shortest possible line between your technical judgment and a capital decision. Read our culture code and are we a good fit? .
 What we offer 
 The physical-AI side of the autonomous grocer, with the capture spec and the first training runs yours from day one
 A data asset few teams in the world get to build, in fresh groceries, a domain as hard as manipulation gets
 Off-the-shelf hardware, a managed cloud estate, and a mandate that has already started
 Benefits — see what we offer 
 Are you in? 
 Instead of a cover letter: pick a published human-video-to-robot-policy pipeline you rate, and tell us where it breaks on a warehouse floor where every hand wears a work glove.

items.jobTitle: Early Careers - Electronics and RF Engineering
items.jobDescription:
Who we are:
 Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards.
As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously.
We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications.
 The Bring Something Amazing Initiative: 
 Helsing’s mission is to protect our democracies. Delivering sovereign AI and mission-critical software capability requires exceptional engineering talent at every level. Following our recent funding and the success of early-career engineers across our teams—including talent from our Formula Student partnerships—we are opening multiple roles across our London and Munich based Physical Products Engineering teams. Traditional recruitment often places artificial barriers in front of early-career builders. Resumes rarely tell the full story of your technical depth, intuition, or drive. To solve this, we are piloting a direct, craft-first hiring path: Bring Something Awesome to Apply (BSA2A).
(This route is designed specifically for early-career engineers. It is entirely optional, you may still apply via our standard job listings if you prefer.)
 Please note that candidates will be considered for the office nearest to them but may also be required to relocate.
 The Process:
 At the core of our technical interview philosophy is Bring Something Awesome (BSA). A dedicated session where candidates present an ambitious technical project they have designed, built, or contributed to.
With BSA2A, we are bringing this step to the very front of the application. Instead of an initial CV and recruiter screen, you apply by submitting a short (maximum 10-minute) prerecorded video walkthrough of something technically compelling you have built. We look for:
 Engineering depth & craft: Technically challenging electrical designs. 
 First-principles problem solving: The ability to deconstruct complex technical challenges autonomously. 
 Clear technical communication: The ability to explain the how and why behind your trade-offs succinctly. 
 Candidates selected through BSA2A move into an accelerated, streamlined technical assessment:
 Expression of Interest: Complete the short form below to confirm your eligibility. Our team will review submissions. 
 Video Submission: Eligible candidates receive a private link with detailed guidance to upload their 10-minute BSA walkthrough. Every video is evaluated directly by a Helsing engineer not an algorithm or automated keyword filter. 
 Technical Interviews (2 × 60 mins): 
 Round 1: BSA Deep Dive. An interactive, technical exploration of your project and system trade-offs.
Round 2: Requirements and Design Interview. Practical, real-world scenario and problem-solving task.
Final Interview (30 mins): A conversation with engineering leadership focused on mission alignment, collaboration, and how you work.
 Note: The initial form below is simply an expression of interest. You do not need your video recorded to submit this form. If your profile is eligible, we will send you dedicated instructions and a submission window. 
 Why apply via this route?
 Evaluated on proof of work, not pedigree: Your designs, choices, and technical curiosity take centre stage—not university ranking, buzzwords, or CV formatting. 
 Play to your strengths: Your application is assessed directly by Helsing engineers on what you can actually build, not how well you format a CV. Putting your real-world work front and centre gives you the highest signal—and the highest probability of success. 
 Accelerated timeline: A focused, high-signal path that bypasses standard preliminary screens and reduces the overall interview cycle by two full stages. 
 The role:
 At Helsing we develop and deliver AI-based capabilities and the enabling infrastructure that allow semi-autonomous platforms to localise, navigate, and perceive the world in real time. We build software that is subject to significant and unorthodox technical constraints, must operate in a wide variety of constantly-changing environments, and has to support an ever-growing list of challenging use-cases. What we build ultimately ends up in the hands of real people in high-risk, high-stress situations, so must be both reliable and frictionless. Taken together, this brings a whole host of interesting engineering challenges across a wide variety of fields that you’ll help us solve.
 The Day-to-Day:
 Find more information on the day-to-day:
Electronics Engineer
 Please note, you need to apply via this page to be considered for the BSA2A process.
 You should apply if you:
 Have designed and integrated electrical and electronic systems in a ideally within aerospace or a similarly demanding domain. 
 Are proficient in PCB design and layout, with hands-on experience using ECAD tools such as Altium Designer or KiCad and simulation tools such as LTSpice 
 Can interpret complex third-party datasheets and technical documentation, translating electrical characteristics and constraints into sound, well-reasoned design decisions 
 Have experience designing cable harnesses and defining communication interfaces. 
 Have worked with RF or radio systems in a hardware integration context. 
 Have experience defining communication interfaces, using this to design harnesses in both 2D and 3D environments and produced 2D formboard drawings that a supplier can build from without interpretation. 
 Are proficient in SOLIDWORKS Electrical and/or Siemens Capital, and have experience managing harness data within a PLM environment to maintain traceability across design, manufacturing and supplier outputs. 
 Have comprehensive connector and interconnect knowledge contacts, backshells, shield terminations, wire types and can specify the right solution for a given mechanical and electrical environment. 
 Understand EMC at the harness level, including how routing decisions, shield termination choices and cable segregation translate directly into platform-level emissions performance. 
 Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.
 Nice to Have
 Have experience with ECAD/MCAD co-design workflows and the integration of electrical systems into complex electromechanical assemblies 
 Have contributed to reliability or safety analyses such as FMEA in a production or pre-production engineering context. 
 Experience with additional harness tools such as Zuken E3.series or CATIA Electrical. 
 Familiarity with harness routing in carbon fibre composite airframes, where grounding continuity and shielding behaviour differ from metallic structures. 
 Exposure to high G-Loading environments. 
 Experience with configuration management and change control in a regulated hardware development programme. 
 Knowledge and/or experience of designing and building electronic subassemblies and their wiring solutions to aerospace standards. 
 Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields 
 Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns 
 The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world 
 Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation, be it reinforcement learning, distributed systems, generative AI, or deployment infrastructure. The defence industry is entering the most exciting phase of the technological development curve. Advances in our field of world are not incremental: Helsing is part of, and often leading, historic leaps forward 
 In our domain, success is a matter of order-of-magnitude improvements and novel capabilities. This means we take bets, aim high, and focus on big opportunities. Despite being a relatively young company, Helsing has already been selected for multiple significant government contracts 
 We actively encourage healthy, proactive, and diverse debate internally about what we do and how we choose to do it. Teams and individual engineers are trusted (and encouraged) to practise responsible autonomy and critical thinking, and to focus on outcomes, not conformity. At Helsing you will have a say in how we (and you!) work, the opportunity to engage on what does and doesn’t work, and to take ownership of aspects of our culture that you care deeply about 
 What we offer
 Competitive salary and VSOP options 
 Relocation support: up to €2,500 and 4 weeks temporary accommodation 
 Learning: €500/£450 yearly allowance 
 Health & wellness: gym membership and mental health support (Nilo.health) 
 Social: regular company events and monthly social allowances 
 Enhanced parental leave: 22 weeks fully paid for primary caregivers & 6 weeks for secondary caregivers 
 Family support: 5 days of paid family emergency leave, 100% remote work option during pregnancy and phased return to work 
 A hands-on onboarding program (affectionately labelled “Infraduction”), in which you will be building tooling and applications to be used across the company. This is your opportunity to learn our tech stack, explore the company, and learn how we get things done - all whilst working with other engineering teams from day one 
 Helsing is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability or gender identity. Please do not submit personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, data concerning your health, or data concerning your sexual orientation.
 Helsing's Candidate Privacy and Confidentiality Regime can be found here.

WISSENSCHAFTL. PROJEKT­KOORDINATOR*IN FÜR DEN AUFBAU DES FORSCHUNGS­ZENTRUMS DIGITAL AI‑DRIVEN SUSTAINABLE VALUE CHAINS (DAISI) Die Hochschule Osnabrück ist die forschungs­stärkste Hochschule für angewandte Wissen­schaften in Niedersachsen. Im Rahmen ihrer strategischen Exzellenz­initiative „Transformation Through Excellence in Applied Sciences“ (TExAS) stärkt sie herausragende Forschungs­profile in drei neuen Forschungs­zentren, die projekt­basiert für drei Jahre aus Mitteln der VolkswagenStiftung gefördert werden.
 Für das neue Forschungs­zentrum „Digital AI-Driven Sustainable Value Chains“ (DAISI) suchen wir Sie zum nächst­möglichen Zeitpunkt als wissen­schaftl. Projekt­koordinator*in. In einem Team von 12 Wissen­schaftler*innen mit exzellenter Vernetzung in der nationalen und internationalen Fachcommunity und im wirtschaftlichen und gesell­schaftlichen Umfeld tragen Sie zur nachhaltigen Profilierung des Forschungs­zentrums in der Hochschul­landschaft bei.
 IHRE AUFGABEN Wissen­schaftliche und operative Koordination des Aufbaus des Forschungs­zentrums: insbesondere Aufbau der Förder-Roadmap, Koordination von Forschungs­anträgen und von Kooperationen mit Partnern aus Wissen­schaft und Wirtschaft; strategische Weiter­entwicklung; Organisation von Gremien­sitzungen, Veranstaltungen und Öffentlichkeits­arbeit; Mitwirkung am Promotionskolleg und an Forschungs­kolloquien
 Konzept­entwicklung/​​‑implementation für die methodische Begleitung und den Transfer der Forschungs­ergebnisse
 Begleitung des Aufbaus des Forschungs­zentrums durch wissen­schaftliche Projekt­arbeiten: thematisch mit Bezug zur Kopplung heterogener Systemtheorien zu konsistenten Multi-Modellen und deren KI‑gestützter Optimierung; Validierung an Industrie­daten und Weiter­entwicklung des Methodenkerns der zentrumseigenen Open-Source-Plattform; Publikation der Ergebnisse in einschlägigen Peer-Review-Journals
 IHR PROFIL abgeschlossenes wissen­schaftliches Hochschul­studium sowie möglichst abgeschlossene Promotion in Informatik, Wirtschafts­informatik, Data Science, Ingenieurwissen­schaften, Automatisierungs­technik oder einem verwandten Fachbereich
 gute Kenntnisse in der formalen Modellierung und Analyse dynamischer Systeme sowie in aktuellen Verfahren der Künstlichen Intelligenz; sicherer Umgang mit Python sowie kollaborativer Software­entwicklung
 Erfahrung in der Beantragung und Durch­führung von Drittmittel­projekten und Verbund­vorhaben mit einer Vielzahl von Partner*innen; bitte benennen Sie in Ihrer Bewerbung Programme, Rollen und Ergebnisse
 Publikations­erfahrung in wissen­schaftlichen, peer-reviewed Journals
 eigenständige und strukturierte Arbeits­weise sowie ein hohes Maß an Team- und Kommunikations­fähigkeit in einem multidisziplinären Team

 Erfahrung mit großen nationalen und europäischen Förder­programmen (DFG, Horizon Europe, Interreg) oder in internationalen Konsortien

 As a Staff Hardware System Test Engineer, you'll develop manufacturing test solutions for complex compute systems. Your work will help ensure products reach customers with the quality and reliability expected from Graphcore.
 You'll shape how hardware is tested across Host Processor Modules, server blades, and multi-node racks. The tools, test content, and diagnostics you create will directly influence manufacturing efficiency and product quality.
 You'll develop test software, design test approaches, and solve challenging hardware issues. You'll work closely with hardware, firmware, software, and manufacturing teams to improve test coverage and diagnose problems quickly.
 This role offers broad technical scope across silicon, boards, systems, software, and manufacturing. You'll have the opportunity to influence engineering decisions and raise technical standards across the organisation.
 The team and culture
 The Product Test and Diagnosis team owns the strategy for finding and diagnosing hardware defects throughout the product lifecycle. The team works across silicon, boards, servers, and rack-scale systems.
 Day to day, engineers work closely with design, firmware, software, quality, and manufacturing teams. Problems are solved through data, technical debate, and hands-on investigation.
 You'll join a global engineering group spanning the UK, Taiwan, India, and the United States. People are trusted to take ownership, make decisions, and drive improvements that deliver measurable results.
 What we're looking for
 Essential:   
 Significant  experience  developing and deploying manufacturing test solutions for high-performance servers, accelerators (GPU-class), or comparable large-scale  compute  hardware. 
 Strong technical leadership as an individual contributor,  with experience  owning  substantial  technical workstreams  and  collaborating  across multiple teams without direct line management responsibility. 
 Strong  technical understanding across silicon, board, and system design sufficient to define effective manufacturing test coverage and lead complex debug/root-cause analysis. 
 Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, with experience  working with internal software/firmware/platform teams to enable testability and diagnosability. 
 Hands-on experience using Linux, OpenBMC , and vendor-specific test tools, diagnostics, and system-level utilities to test hardware in lab and manufacturing environments. 
 Strong software engineering skills with scripting and automation (e.g., Python, Bash, or similar), including building reliable test infrastructure and integrating heterogeneous test content.   
 Desirable   
 Familiarity with rack-scale/multi-node systems, high-speed interconnects, and production qualification of complex assemblies. 
 Experience improving manufacturing KPIs (yield, test time, false fail reduction) through data-driven test optimisation and robust statistical/diagnostic approaches. 
 Knowledge of open-source tools commonly used for manufacturing test, system bring-up, and hardware diagnostics. 
 Experience designing testability/diagnosability features into products (e.g., telemetry, self-test hooks, debug interfaces) in partnership with design teams.   
 Benefits
 Unlimited annual leave
 Up to 5% matched pension
 Phantom equity – share in Graphcore’s success
 True flexibility in how and where you work
 Office spaces designed for collaboration
 Free food and an on-site barista
 Health cash plan
 Income protection
 Life assurance

 Join the Team at Graphcore
 Graphcore is building the compute platform for the next generation of artificial intelligence. From advanced silicon to intelligent software, our technology is designed to unlock breakthroughs in AI and bring its benefits to every industry.
 As part of the SoftBank Group, we’re backed by one of the world’s most ambitious technology investors, working alongside companies shaping the future of AI. Together, we share a bold goal: to help enable artificial superintelligence and ensure it delivers meaningful impact at a global scale.
 At Graphcore, you’ll work with people who are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Our teams bring together AI researchers, chip designers, software engineers and systems experts from a wide range of backgrounds. It’s an environment where we take on big challenges with curiosity and focus, move quickly and decisively, take real ownership of our work, and speak up to challenge ideas, stepping up to support each other and lead through action.
 If you enjoy solving complex hardware challenges and want to influence how advanced AI systems are tested and delivered, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now to join Graphcore.

About Griffin 
 Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.
 We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.
 We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.
 Learn more about what we do 
 Our culture 
 We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.
 We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.
 We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.
 Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.
 Learn more about our culture. 
 The team 
 Infrastructure sits within the Craft function. We’re a small team of three - two engineers and an engineering manager - who work closely with our CTO and Founder, Allen Rohner . It’s our job to build the foundations that everything else at Griffin runs on: the systems, the tooling, the automation that helps us run a highly resilient and reliable platform and lets other teams ship fast. We're a software engineering team as much as an infrastructure team: we write the code that runs our platform, not just the configuration around it.
 When we start work, we explore multiple solutions before picking one. We write RFCs, build proof-of-concepts, and run experiments to validate approaches. Once we commit to building something, we care about maintainability more than cleverness, observability more than hoping it works, and scalability over premature optimisation. We take the necessary time to ship quality solutions rather than hitting arbitrary deadlines. Once something goes live, we refactor the rough edges rather than polish what's already working.
 The opportunity 
 Day to day, you'll build and manage the infrastructure the bank runs on - both in the cloud and on our own hardware in third party data centres. This means running FoundationDB clusters and writing the software and tooling for hitless upgrades, managing Kubernetes, writing infrastructure as code in Pulumi and CDK, running the Bazel build farm, and owning the deployment pipeline from CI to production.
 Operational resilience is a big part of the job: replica clusters, multi-region failover, and chaos engineering to test how systems handle failures. Security access, CircleCI pipelines, DataDog integration, and cloud spend all fall under infrastructure too.
 On our roadmap currently is: building out our self-hosted infrastructure to support a hybrid-cloud setup and remove single-vendor reliance, improving how Kubernetes scales, improving the build farm, and building out our PKI infrastructure. We also have plans for a global HTTP routing layer to allow seamless failover between sites. Much of this is software we built ourselves, and you'll shape it from the first design through to production.
 Our infrastructure as code is written in TypeScript. Where it makes sense, tooling gets written in Clojure. There's some Rust too.
 What success looks like 
 Infrastructure problems become production problems fast. Success here means thinking ahead - identifying issues with scale, security, or compliance before they affect services.
 You've eliminated an entire class of incidents by fixing the underlying architectural issue. You've proven the database and compute platform can handle 10x current traffic volumes by working with backend teams to stress-test it. You've cut deploy times in half by rethinking how the pipeline works. You've tested multi-region failover under realistic failure scenarios and it worked. 
 You've shipped well-tested software that turns risky manual operations, like database upgrades, into routine, hitless ones that the whole team maintains with confidence.
 You've redesigned service discovery to remove networking issues that used to cause weekly firefights. When new FCA requirements dropped, you were already compliant because you'd built the infrastructure to handle it months earlier.
 To do this, you'll own 
 Infrastructure architecture decisions - how we structure our systems, what approaches we take, what tools we build
 Production reliability - keeping the database, compute, build farm, and deployment pipelines running and improving them
 What other teams depend on to ship - CI/CD, security access, monitoring integration, and the infrastructure that lets engineers deploy safely
 Infrastructure cost and efficiency - managing spend and resource usage across AWS and DataDog
 Infrastructure software - the code behind our database control plane, operational tooling and automation, from design and implementation through to testing, code review and maintenance
 Stack: FoundationDB, Kubernetes, Bazel, Pulumi, CDK, CircleCI, DataDog, Clojure, TypeScript
 Your background 
 You'll fit in well here if you have:
 Solid systems experience - you've run container orchestration in production, written infrastructure as code, and understand IP networking well enough to debug it when things go wrong
 Cloud infrastructure experience - you've built and managed production environments, worked with networking, identity management, and compute at scale
 Strong software engineering fundamentals - you write code to solve problems, and you're as comfortable designing, testing and reviewing production software as you are configuring infrastructure. TypeScript, Python, Go, or functional languages are all fine. If your experience only extends to Bash scripting and YAML, we probably aren't a good fit for you
 Comfort with startup environments - small teams, shifting priorities, high autonomy
 We write a lot of our tooling in Clojure - our database control plane, operational scripts, and automation. You don't need Clojure experience coming in, but you'll need to learn it once you're here. If you've worked with functional languages before, that helps.
 Regardless, you should be comfortable picking up new languages and approaches as we do find ourselves reading through the codebases of open-source systems and tools we use to understand their behaviour, and they are written in a diverse range of languages we don't use ourselves.
 What can we offer you? 
 We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.
 Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK
 Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year
 Time off: 28 days’ holiday + bank holidays 
 Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together
 Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme
 Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG
 Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva
 Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service
 AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools
 Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.
 As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks.
 How do I apply? 
 Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.
 We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs.
 Under representation 
 At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

About Us 
 1GLOBAL is a technology-driven global mobile communications provider helping enterprises and consumer brands deliver seamless connectivity worldwide. Powered by a best-in-class telecom platform, proprietary eSIM technology, and its own mobile core network across 15 countries, 1GLOBAL operates as a fully regulated telecommunications provider in 43 countries.
Founded in 2022, 1GLOBAL has rapidly become one of Europe's fastest-growing telecom technology companies, connecting more than 80 million people and devices globally. Our customers include leading banks, multinational enterprises, global retailers, travel companies, payment service providers, and digital-first businesses.
Headquartered in the Netherlands, with R&D hubs in Lisbon, Berlin, and São Paulo, 1GLOBAL employs over 550 professionals across 16 countries. With annual revenues exceeding US$200 million and a strong track record of profitability, we continue to invest in innovation, infrastructure, and international expansion as we redefine the future of global mobile connectivity.
 About the DevOps department 
 Our DevOps department has three teams. Each owns one layer of the platform:
 Foundations (ROOT): machines, operating systems, virtualisation, VPNs and databases.
 Cloud-Native Infra (CLOUD): cloud accounts, Kubernetes clusters, networking, identity and shared platform services.
 Developer Experience (DEVX): pipelines, GitOps, internal tooling, observability and APIs used by engineering teams every day.
About the Team 
 DEVX builds the tools and workflows our engineering teams use to ship software. That covers pipelines, GitOps, internal CLIs, observability and API management. Our tooling is written in Go.
 We own: GitLab CI pipelines, Stack CLIs and internal tooling, Argo CD, Crossplane Compositions, metrics, logs, tracing, profiling, alerts and dashboards, API management, OAuth2 clients and the Governance API, our internal developer platform
 We don't own: cloud accounts, clusters, networking, the service mesh, Crossplane providers and XRDs (CLOUD), GitLab instance upgrades and VMs.
 Your first 6 months 
 Improve observability across the platform: alert quality, performance and data-transfer optimisation.
 Take ownership of our Internal tools and the shared pipeline templates our developers use.
 Help migrating the remaining deployments to GitOps with Argo CD.
 About the role 
 Develop Internal tools in Go.
 Own metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards, and help teams decide what to measure.
 Build and maintain GitLab CI pipelines and shared templates.
 Run Argo CD and GitOps workflows across environments.
 Write Crossplane Compositions on top of XRDs.
 Manage APIs, OAuth2 clients and the Governance API.
 Help shape our internal developer platform.
 Requirements
 Requirements 
 About You 
 Must Have 
 5+ years in DevOps, infrastructure or platform engineering, including ownership of production systems and on-call.
 You write design docs, reason about trade-offs, and mentor other engineers.
 Fluent English, written and spoken. Please send your CV in English.
 Solid fundamentals in compute, networking and storage, and you're at home on Linux.
 Go as your main language: production code with tests and releases, and CLIs or services you maintain.
 Observability: Grafana, Prometheus, Thanos, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope and alerts that people actually trust.
 GitLab CI at scale: shared templates, includes, runners, pipeline security.
 Helm and Kustomize.
 Kubernetes from the workload side: CRDs and debugging deployments.
 You treat developers as customers, with clear docs, feedback loops and attention to adoption.
Nice to Have 
 OpenTelemetry or distributed tracing (Tempo, Jaeger).
 Argo CD/GitOps: ApplicationSets, sync strategies, promotion between environments.
 OAuth2/OIDC, JWTs, API management.
 Python as a second language.
 Crossplane Compositions
 Multi-stage Docker builds and image hygiene.
 Writing Operators (kubebuilder/controller-runtime)
 REST API design
 Benefits 
 Why 1GLOBAL? 
 Growth Opportunities: Advance your career in one of the fastest growing telecommunications companies, expanding over 50% year-on-year under the leadership of successful tech entrepreneurs.
 Major Transaction Exposure: Be in the driver’s seat for transactions that will have an impact on the future telco industry.
 Work with a Talented Team: From the Board and the Founders to the Senior Management Team, you will collaborate daily with the most capable and renowned external advisors and constantly being exposed to talented and driven individuals.
 Dynamic Work Environment: Thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced workplace where innovation is encouraged, and every contribution counts.
 Professional Development: Work alongside industry experts to enhance your skills and knowledge in a cutting-edge field.
 International Experience: Gain opportunities to work in different 1GLOBAL offices around the world as you grow within the company.
 Open Communication Culture: Join a team where your ideas are heard, and open dialogue is encouraged, fostering a supportive and transparent work environment.
 Get Things Done Attitude: Be part of a results-driven team that values efficiency, creativity, and the drive to make a tangible impact in the industry.
1GLOBAL is an equal opportunity employer, we value your character as much as your talent. Diversity drives our innovation, and we offer a collaborative, dynamic, and international work environment. We are excited for you to join our mission to revolutionise connectivity globally.

About AlphaSense:  
 AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com . Come join us. 
 About the Team:
 The Cloud DX team owns the outer loop of software development at AlphaSense, everything from the moment code is pushed to source control to the moment it reaches production, for ~400 engineers distributed across the globe. We've built a solid delivery foundation and we're now raising the bar toward industry-leading CI/CD. Progressive delivery, canary deployments, automated rollbacks, trunk-based development, GitOps workflows: these aren't aspirations but the direction we're actively building, and we're looking for passionate engineers to help shape what best-in-class looks like.
 About the Role: 
 This is a Staff Engineer role with real breadth. It requires both operational and software development skills, the ability to lead projects and collaborate across timezones with Engineering leaders and very senior Engineers across dozens of teams. You'll design and operate production-grade delivery infrastructure, contribute hands-on in Go and Python, and help shape the engineering practices a global organisation depends on. 
We're looking for someone who genuinely embraces AI tooling in their day-to-day work, appreciates the productivity value it brings, and is motivated to push that further, both in their own practice and by helping embed AI-assisted workflows into the SDLC for the wider engineering organization.
 Who You Are:
 Strong experience in Platform Engineering or Developer Experience roles focused on CI/CD and delivery, ideally at companies with 200+ engineers
 Experience owning and operating a CI/CD platform at admin and architecture level, including security, configuration, and enablement
 Proven ability to design and operate delivery systems at scale
 Hands-on software development experience including production-quality Go
 Passion for progressive delivery practices: canary deployments & automated rollbacks
 Familiarity with cloud-native architectures and Kubernetes-based platforms
 Passion for using AI to improve engineering velocity, quality, and developer experience
 Strong collaboration skills and ability to influence across teams
 [Nice to Have] Built and/or maintained an IDP in production 
 [Nice to Have] Previous experience working in both Software and Platform Engineering teams 
 [Nice to Have] Interest in Security and an understanding of RBAC and OAuth
 What You’ll Do: 
 Own and evolve our CI/CD architecture and the developer-facing experience
 Drive continuous improvements to pipeline reliability, speed, and predictability
 Define paved paths that let product teams ship fast and safely without deep platform knowledge
 Own the delivery process end-to-end, from code merge to production
 Champion progressive delivery practices: canary deployments & automated rollbacks
 Build tooling that makes deployments observable, repeatable, and self-service
 Own and evolve our Internal Developer Portal and the self-service experience around it
 Partner with Cloud Platform teams on infrastructure while owning the developer-facing delivery
 Embed AI tooling into delivery workflows in ways that create lasting productivity gains.
 AlphaSense is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling AlphaSense’s commitment to equal employment opportunity. AlphaSense does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, military or veteran status, disability, or any other non-merit factor. This policy applies to every aspect of employment at AlphaSense, including recruitment, hiring, training, advancement, and termination. 
 In addition, it is the policy of AlphaSense to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works. 
 Recruiting Scams and Fraud 
 We at AlphaSense have been made aware of fraudulent job postings and individuals impersonating AlphaSense recruiters. These scams may involve fake job offers, requests for sensitive personal information, or demands for payment. Please note: 
 AlphaSense never asks candidates to pay for job applications, equipment, or training. 
 All official communications will come from an @ alpha-sense.com  email address. 
 If you’re unsure about a job posting or recruiter, verify it on our  Careers page . 
 If you believe you’ve been targeted by a scam or have any doubts regarding the authenticity of any job listing purportedly from or on behalf of AlphaSense please contact us. Your security and trust matter to us.

Who we are: 
 We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintech companies – on a mission to create the world's most empowering way to pay.
 We launched the product in 2020 and achieved double unicorn status, valued at $2 billion, and since then have taken on more than 6 million customers.
 Our mission is to become the best way to pay for anything, anywhere and say goodbye to credit costs for everyone. This is huge. Want to join us?
 The Role: 
 We are looking for an IAM Engineer to support day-to-day identity and access management operations, primarily using Okta Workforce Identity Cloud. This is a hands-on role suited to someone beginning their IAM career or developing from an IT support or security operations position. You will help manage secure access to SaaS, cloud and internal systems, with structured guidance from experienced IAM and security engineers.
 You will support joiner, mover and leaver processes, application access requests, Okta troubleshooting and role-based access control (RBAC). You will also gain practical exposure to Terraform-managed IAM configuration through peer-reviewed changes and established deployment processes.
 What you’ll do: 
 Process and fulfil approved access requests, user onboarding, transfers and offboarding in Okta and connected applications.
 Assist with Okta user, group, application assignment and MFA enrolment administration, following documented procedures.
 Support role-based and group-based access assignments in line with least-privilege and approval requirements.
 Perform first-line troubleshooting for SSO login failures, MFA issues, account lockouts and provisioning errors; escalate complex cases.
 Check and reconcile access records, provisioning status and leaver deprovisioning outcomes, raising exceptions promptly.
 Support regular access reviews, entitlement checks and collection of evidence for internal and external audits.
 Assist with onboarding applications to Okta by gathering requirements and testing SAML, OIDC or SCIM integrations under supervision.
 Review and make simple, approved Terraform configuration changes to Okta groups or application assignments, using version control and peer review.
 Follow change control, ticketing, documented runbooks and security incident escalation procedures.
 Keep IAM tickets, knowledge articles, configuration records and operational documentation accurate and current.
 Work with IT, Security, HR and application owners to resolve routine identity issues and identify recurring problems.
 What we're looking for: 
 Some practical experience in IT support, service desk, systems administration, security operations or IAM; relevant placements or apprenticeships considered.
 Basic familiarity with Okta or another identity provider, including users, groups, single sign-on and multifactor authentication.
 Understanding of access requests, approvals, account provisioning, deprovisioning and the joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle.
 Awareness of RBAC, least privilege and the importance of separating privileged and standard access.
 Ability to follow runbooks, manage tickets carefully and document changes and troubleshooting clearly.
 Familiarity with Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, Google Workspace or comparable directory services.
 Basic knowledge of SAML, OIDC or SCIM concepts, or a willingness to develop these skills.
 Interest in Infrastructure as Code and Terraform; prior production Terraform experience is not required.
 Good communication, attention to detail, customer service and willingness to learn from senior engineers.
 Bonus skills: 
 Exposure to Okta Workforce Identity Cloud or an Okta Certified Professional learning pathway.
 Introductory Terraform knowledge, including reading plans, understanding resources and using Git pull requests.
 Experience supporting enterprise SaaS applications such as Microsoft 365, GitHub, Atlassian or Slack.
 Familiarity with SCIM provisioning or HR-driven joiner/mover/leaver workflows.
 Awareness of ISO 27001, SOC 2, Cyber Essentials Plus or GDPR-related access controls.
 Basic PowerShell, Python, Bash, REST API or automation experience.
 Understanding of phishing-resistant MFA, privileged access controls and secure handling of identities.

 Okta Workforce Identity Cloud (users, groups, applications and MFA)

About Zego 🚀 
 At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.
Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.
 We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖
 For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook.
We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.
 Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor .
 If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring. 
 Purpose of the role 🎯
 We're looking for a Data Engineer to join our data engineering function, helping to build and maintain the data platform that powers Zego's ambitious growth.
 This is a hands-on technical role. You'll build and maintain scalable, reliable, and secure data pipelines, working within an established platform and architecture. You'll work closely with peers across Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, and Product to ensure our data infrastructure is efficient and reliable.
 AI is central to how we work at Zego, and that extends to engineering. You'll be encouraged to use AI tools to move faster, automate the routine, and focus your time on the problems that matter most, while staying thoughtful about where and how they add value.
You'll learn from experienced engineers across the team, and you'll be encouraged to grow your technical skills while contributing to high-quality, well-tested work.
 What you will be doing 🛠️
 Technical Delivery 
 Build, maintain, and improve data pipelines and related systems.
 Follow and help uphold best practices in data engineering, including testing, CI/CD, observability, and infrastructure as code.
 Take part in code reviews and team knowledge sharing.
 Platform & Data 
 Build and maintain data pipelines, warehouses, and streaming systems within our existing architecture.
 Ensure data is modelled and structured to meet the needs of analytics, data science, and operational use cases.
 Contribute to improvements in our data systems and tooling.
 Collaboration & Delivery 
 Work with teams across the business to understand requirements and turn them into reliable technical solutions.
 Help identify opportunities for optimisation and tool improvements.
 Deliver against the technical roadmap for data engineering.
 What you will need to be successful 🏆 
 Experience: 2+ years as a Data Engineer working on data platforms, ideally in product-led or high-growth environments.
 Technical Skills: 
 Experience building and operating ETL/ELT pipelines.
 Hands-on experience with modern data stacks — our tech includes Python, SQL, Snowflake, Apache Iceberg, AWS S3, PostgresDB, Airflow, dbt, and Apache Spark, deployed via AWS, Docker, and Terraform (experience with some of these or similar technologies is expected).
 Collaboration: Ability to work effectively with teammates and stakeholders.
 Problem-Solving: Pragmatic approach to balancing quality with delivery needs.
 Growth Mindset: Eagerness to learn, take feedback, and grow your technical skills.
 You work AI-first. You will use AI daily here, and we mean daily. You do not need to arrive an expert, but you do need to arrive curious, experiment fast, and take ownership of getting good quickly. People who wait to be trained will find this uncomfortable.
 Nice to Have: 
 Familiarity with Data Mesh or Lakehouse architectures.
 Familiarity with Kubernetes, Docker, and real-time streaming technologies (e.g. Kafka, Kinesis).
 Exposure to ML engineering pipelines or MLOps frameworks.
 The Zego ways of working 🏡 
 Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our office (central London, Gibraltar or Halifax) weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It's about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.
 We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It's a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year.
 Here is what the last one looked like .
 Benefits 🎁 
 💰 Market-competitive salary, benchmarked against your function and reviewed every year.
 🏆 Annual performance bonus, linked to company performance and your contribution.
 📈 Share options, a real stake in the company and a share in the future you build
 🩺 Private medical insurance.
 🏖️ Pension, generous holiday, and £1,000 a year to spend on getting to the office or learning something new.
 💻 Cutting-edge systems and tools, so you always have what you need to drive your impact.
 Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? We want to hear from you.
 Zego, leading the AI evolution in insurance. 
 Equal opportunities 🌈

Building the Future of Open Finance 
 Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.
 The team 
 Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.
   The opportunity 
 Make web development faster by improving builds, type checking, linting, and tests, both locally and in CI
 Evolve our monorepo, package management, and shared configuration so changes across applications and libraries are straightforward and reliable
 Simplify development environment setup and support parallel work by engineers and coding agents, with clear documentation and tools that work with minimal configuration
 Improve web delivery pipelines, including preview environments, progressive rollouts, production monitoring, and reliable rollback
 Strengthen automated validation, including browser-based checks that help engineers and agents verify changes before they ship
 Work with product and infrastructure teams to investigate web performance, improve observability, and address problems across application code, tooling, and delivery
 Lead tooling upgrades and migrations across teams, balancing long-term improvements with the practical needs of engineers shipping products
 Own improvements from design through rollout and ongoing maintenance, staying close to the people using what you build
     What you bring 
 Solid experience building and maintaining production web applications, with a strong understanding of React and the modern JavaScript ecosystem
 Strong TypeScript and JavaScript skills, including experience using Node.js to build tooling and automation
 A good understanding of how web applications work, including browser behavior, module systems, bundling, caching, and performance
 Experience improving developer tooling, build systems, automated testing, or CI/CD pipelines, and the ability to diagnose problems across those layers
 Good judgment about reliability, security, maintainability, and when added complexity is worth the cost
 The ability to lead a technical design, explain it clearly, and work with other teams to get changes adopted
 Ownership: you can take an ambiguous problem, find a practical solution, and keep it working once people depend on it
     Nice to haves 
 Experience maintaining large monorepos, shared packages, or tooling used by multiple engineering teams
 Familiarity with pnpm, ESM, and modern build, linting, and test tools
 Experience with browser automation, end-to-end testing, web performance profiling, or production observability
 Hands-on experience with coding agents and improving the environments, documentation, and feedback loops they rely on
 Experience with GitLab CI, containers, or cloud infrastructure supporting web development and delivery
 Contributions to open-source frontend infrastructure or developer tools
 Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. 
 Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. 
 We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. 
 Our commitment 
 Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

Partner Solutions Engineer 
 At Phrase, we help open the door to global business by providing the world's leading Language Intelligence Platform.
 The Phrase Platform combines AI, agentic orchestration, and a headless, API-first architecture in one composable system. Beyond translation, it orchestrates and adapts content to culture, audience, channel, brand voice, and intended outcome in any language, for every audience. It applies the context that makes content perform in every market: quality standards, glossaries, prior translations, and cultural nuance. Every team, in every region, can ship content that is on-brand, on-point, and ready for any audience.
 Phrase gives enterprises the intelligence to automate workflows, the freedom to connect their own tools and engines, and the control to govern global content at scale.
 With a global team based in our offices, and remote colleagues across Europe, the UK, the US, and the APAC region, Phrase offers an international environment built on collaboration, innovation, and shared purpose.
 Partner Solutions Engineer is a new role in Solutions Engineering, built to help agencies make AI useful in their clients' global content workflows. You will lead the solutions side of partner-led deals from the first conversation to close, working alongside Partnerships, who lead on commercials. The people you meet are production and technology teams in agencies, language service providers and martech and AI platforms, who work in content operations and want answers quickly. You will report to the VP, Solutions Engineering, and work exclusively on partner-led deals, helping to shape how the role works as it grows. 
 This is a global role: we would ideally like you based in the UK or Western Europe and working on UK time, but we are flexible for the right person.
 What you'll be responsible for: 
 Lead the solutions side of partner-led opportunities from first conversation to close, while Partnerships leads on commercials
 Find the business problem a partner and their client are trying to solve before showing the product, explain where Phrase fits and be clear about trade-offs
 Turn Phrase's technical detail into a clear value case that a senior marketer would buy and an agency would pitch
 Run demos and hands-on co-innovation sessions with partners using Phrase integrations across CMSs and DXPs, CRM and marketing platforms, creative tools and developer tools
 Show how Phrase works inside AI assistants and agentic workflows through the Phrase MCP Server and Phrase Atlas, and help partners build on Phrase through our APIs
 Work with Product to co-design differentiated integrations with partners, and bring what you hear from agencies and platforms into the roadmap so those integrations are adopted, stay in use and drive revenue
 Run workshops that take a partner team from no knowledge of Phrase to confident in a single session, at partner offices, our events and theirs
 Build working relationships with production, technology and practice leads inside partner organisations
 Work alongside Solutions Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering and Product, and bring them in early for deep technical or build work
 Share what you learn from partners with Product and Partnerships so that our integrations and partner programme keep improving
 Present the whole Phrase Language Intelligence Platform: projects, vendors and workflows in Phrase TMS with Phrase Orchestrator automating the steps in between; brand terms and tone of voice across markets; developer access through our APIs, Phrase Strings and the Phrase MCP Server; and transcription, subtitling and dubbing in Phrase Studio
 What you need: 
 At least three years in solutions consulting, solutions engineering or similar pre-sales in martech (CMS, DXP, marketing automation or content platform), or leading technology conversations at an agency
 Deep experience in at least one CMS, DXP, content or marketing platform, and the ability to map a client's stack and explain the choices to agency and marketing teams
 High emotional intelligence and conversational skill, so that one-to-one and group meetings feel fluid with you in them, and the habit of asking great questions and reading the room as the conversation moves
 The ability to walk into an agency meeting with little or no customer context and still make it a great conversation, as ambiguity and last-minute briefings are normal in this work
 The ability to lead a room: whiteboard a session, ask good questions about the business problem, and frame technical detail as outcomes a senior marketer cares about
 Confidence running live demos and adapting them to the people in the room
 An understanding of how agencies and holding companies staff, sell and deliver work for their clients, and how generative AI is changing that work
 Working knowledge of APIs and webhooks, the ability to sketch a workable integration and explain the trade-offs to non-technical people, and an understanding of where AI agents and MCP fit
 Clear, friendly written and spoken English
 Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time for partner meetings and events, sometimes across time zones
 Experience in localisation, transcreation or language technology (desirable). We are just as open to people from martech, or from agency and martech, who pick up new technology quickly and want to learn the language side with us
 Experience at a headless CMS or content platform, in an agency technology role, or at or closely with a holding company's production arm, a systems integrator or a language service provider (desirable)
 Hands-on experience with an MCP client or with building on LLM APIs (desirable)
 A second language, or experience speaking at events or running training sessions (desirable)
 Our current tech stack in this role: 
 Phrase TMS
 Phrase Orchestrator
 Phrase Strings
 Phrase Studio
 Phrase MCP Server
 Phrase Atlas
 Phrase APIs and webhooks
 Phrase integrations with CMSs and DXPs, CRM and marketing platforms, creative tools and developer tools
 What you'll get: 
 Work experience in a successful and growing global SaaS company
 Be part of an international team in Europe, APAC, and the Americas
 Expert colleagues in their field who are determined to build the best localization platform on the market, creating a world where language never limits opportunity
 An agile work environment, where it is encouraged to take smart risks
 Take part in a culture full of trust, support and loyalty, where respectful and open feedback is valued, and diversity is fully embraced
 A positive, open-minded, and innovative atmosphere
 Support in your professional development and personal career goals
 What's on top: 
 4 Company holidays additional to your regular holidays (1 day per quarter where the entire company is off to celebrate our achievements).
 In addition, the company also provides employees with a Christmas break to allow you to spend time with family and friends without use of your vacation allocation.
 Your birthday is off because it is important to celebrate you as well.
 2 Giveback days where you can support the local community, volunteer, and/or participate in charity events and activities.
 Professional and extensive onboarding.
 Enterprise Claude Licence
 Additional local benefits depending on the entity you're hired at, just ask your Talent Acquisition Partner
